items.title: [v2] macOS: each MenuUpdateApplicationMenu / MenuSetApplicationMenu leaks the whole previous menu tree
items.body:
Wails version family: v2
Exact Wails version: v2.17.0 (the darwin menu files on master are unchanged)
Operating System: macOS

### Description

On macOS, every call to `runtime.MenuUpdateApplicationMenu` or `runtime.MenuSetApplicationMenu` builds a new native menu tree, and the previous one is never freed: every `WailsMenu`, `WailsMenuItem` and `NSMenuItem` of every earlier build stays alive. The Go side grows too: each item is added to `idToMenuItem` / `menuItemToID` and never removed.

`MenuItem.SetLabel` only sets the Go field, so the documented way to change a label at runtime ("update the menu struct and call MenuUpdateApplicationMenu", `website/docs/reference/menus.mdx`) rebuilds the whole menu bar. An app that renames an item often (ours names the step in Edit → Undo, e.g. "Undo Move Device", after every edit) leaks a full menu bar each time.

Measured in our app (8 menus, 26 items), rebuilding the menu N times after start-up and counting with `heap <pid>` and `vmmap --summary <pid>`:

| Rebuilds | WailsMenuItem | NSMenuItem | WailsMenu | NSMenu | Physical footprint |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 26 | 28 | 8 | 3 | 29 MB |
| 1,000 | 26,026 | 27,028 | 8,008 | 1,003 | 87 MB |
| 2,000 | 52,026 | 54,028 | 16,008 | 2,003 | 178 MB |

Exactly one full tree per rebuild, unchanged seconds later: about 60–90 KB per rebuild for this menu.

### To Reproduce

1. Any v2 app with an application menu (`options.App.Menu`).
2. Rebuild it repeatedly, for example from `OnDomReady`:
   ```go
   go func() {
       for i := 0; i < 1000; i++ {
           item.SetLabel(fmt.Sprintf("Item %d", i))
           runtime.MenuUpdateApplicationMenu(ctx)
       }
   }()
   ```
3. Compare `heap <pid> | grep -E 'WailsMenuItem|WailsMenu'` before and after.

Our measurement called `runtime.MenuSetApplicationMenu(ctx, sameMenu)` in that loop inside our app; `MenuUpdateApplicationMenu` reaches the same `Window.UpdateApplicationMenu`. The snippet is that pattern reduced; we haven't run it as a standalone app.

### Expected behaviour

The previous menu tree is released when it is replaced, so memory stays flat however often the menu is updated.

### Screenshots

None.

### Attempted Fixes

From reading v2.17.0's `internal/frontend/desktop/darwin/` (its Objective-C is built without ARC):

- `Window.UpdateApplicationMenu` builds a new tree on every call: [window.go#L313-L319](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/v2.17.0/v2/internal/frontend/desktop/darwin/window.go#L313-L319)
- each menu, submenus included, is `[[WailsMenu new] initWithNSTitle:]` and never released: [Application.m#L310-L317](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/v2.17.0/v2/internal/frontend/desktop/darwin/Application.m#L310-L317)
- each item is `[WailsMenuItem new]`, added with `addItem:` and never released: [WailsMenu.m#L127-L157](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/v2.17.0/v2/internal/frontend/desktop/darwin/WailsMenu.m#L127-L157)
- the new tree replaces the old through a `retain` property and `setMainMenu:`, each releasing only its own hold: [WailsContext.h#L57](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/v2.17.0/v2/internal/frontend/desktop/darwin/WailsContext.h#L57), [Application.m#L325-L337](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/v2.17.0/v2/internal/frontend/desktop/darwin/Application.m#L325-L337)
- every item is registered in `idToMenuItem` / `menuItemToID` and never removed: [menuitem.go#L23-L48](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/v2.17.0/v2/internal/frontend/desktop/darwin/menuitem.go#L23-L48)

The same leak in v3's macOS menus was fixed by #5714 ("Every `Menu.Update()` leaked one `NSMenuItem` per item … and one `NSMenu` per submenu"). Carrying that approach back to v2 (release each menu and item made with `new` once its parent holds it, and prune the ID maps while keeping the previous generation for clicks already in flight) would likely fix it.

We plan to work around it by building the menu once and changing items in place through our own cgo (`setTitle:`, `setEnabled:`, `setHidden:` on items in `[NSApp mainMenu]`).

### System Details

macOS 15.7.9, Apple silicon (arm64), Go 1.27.3. The app is built with `go build -tags desktop,production` rather than the Wails CLI, so there is no `wails doctor` output.

Not specific to building without the CLI: `wails build` adds only tags, `-w -s`, a deployment target and frameworks on macOS (no `-fobjc-arc`), and the darwin `.m` files' explicit `release`/`autorelease` calls wouldn't compile under ARC anyway.

### Additional context

Related: #6058 and #6083 (the `Calloc.String` leak on the v2 darwin frontend, fixed in v2.17.0).

items.title: [v3][Windows] OnShutdown hook not called when closing last window on Windows
items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.34

### Operating System

Windows

### Description

 In Wails v3, when closing the application by clicking the close button (`X`) on the last window (with default `DisableQuitOnLastWindowClosed: false`), registered `OnShutdown` hooks (`globalApplication.cleanup()`) are not executed on Windows.

As a result, critical application cleanup routines (such as terminating child processes, closing persistent sockets, or saving application state) are completely bypassed.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a minimal application with an `OnShutdown` hook:

```go
package main

import (
	"log"

	"github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application"
)

func main() {
	app := application.New(application.Options{
		Name: "OnShutdownBug",
		OnShutdown: func() {
			log.Println(">>> OnShutdown CALLED! <<<")
		},
	})

	app.Window.NewWithOptions(application.WebviewWindowOptions{
		Title:  "Test Window",
		Width:  400,
		Height: 300,
	})

	if err := app.Run(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

2. Run on Windows: go run main.go
3. Click the X button on the window title bar to close it.
4. Notice that >>> OnShutdown CALLED! <<< is NEVER printed to the terminal.

(Note: OnShutdown is only called if application code explicitly invokes app.Quit().)


### Expected behaviour

Closing the last window should invoke `m.destroy()` (matching the Linux implementation in `v3/pkg/application/application_linux_gtk3.go`), ensuring that `globalApplication.cleanup()` and registered `OnShutdown` hooks are executed uniformly across Windows, Linux, and macOS.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

Inspected `v3/pkg/application/application_windows.go:353-356`:

```go
func (m *windowsApp) unregisterWindow(w *windowsWebviewWindow) {
    m.windowMapLock.Lock()
    delete(m.windowMap, w.hwnd)
    m.windowMapLock.Unlock()

    // If this was the last window...
    if len(m.windowMap) == 0 &&
    !m.parent.options.Windows.DisableQuitOnLastWindowClosed {
        w32.PostQuitMessage(0) // <-- cleanup() / OnShutdown is skipped here!
    }
}
```

Compared with Linux (v3/pkg/application/application_linux_gtk3.go:162-164):

```go
// If this was the last window...
if len(a.windowMap) == 0 && !a.parent.options.Linux.DisableQuitOnLastWindowClosed
{
    a.destroy()
}
```

And m.destroy() in v3/pkg/application/application_windows.go:196-205:

```go
func (m *windowsApp) destroy() {
    if !globalApplication.shouldQuit() {
        return
    }
    globalApplication.cleanup() // invokes OnShutdown tasks

    // destroy the main thread window
    w32.DestroyWindow(m.mainThreadWindowHWND)

    // Post a quit message to the main thread
    w32.PostQuitMessage(0)
}
```

Changing w32.PostQuitMessage(0) to m.destroy() in unregisterWindow fixes the issue because m.destroy() internally invokes globalApplication.cleanup() before posting w32.PostQuitMessage(0).

### System Details

items.title: [v3] Windows: crash in applyDarkMode after pkg/w32's init frees uxtheme.dll
items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.34

### Operating System

Windows

### Description

On Windows 11 build 26300 with dark mode on, our app (ArrowLoop, https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/arrowloop, module desktop/) crashes with an access violation as soon as its first window is created: Exception 0xc0000005 (execute) at PC=0x7ff8c64a9860. The trace is below.

The init in pkg/w32/theme.go loads uxtheme.dll, takes ordinals 133, 132, 135, 136 and 104 with GetProcAddressByOrdinal, keeps the addresses in the package-level funcs, and calls windows.FreeLibrary(localUXTheme) at the end (theme.go:164). Nothing else holds uxtheme.dll at that point, so the DLL is unloaded. In a minimal v3 app on the same machine, GetModuleHandleEx("uxtheme.dll") fails right after application.New and again after Window.NewWithOptions. In this boot ordinal 133 (AllowDarkModeForWindow) sits at 0x7ff8c64a9860, which is exactly the crashing PC, so the call in applyDarkMode (webview_window_windows.go:1567) jumps into the unloaded DLL.

Whether an app crashes depends on whether something maps uxtheme.dll again before the first applyDarkMode call. Our app hits it on every start, the release build included. A minimal app with one window on the same machine does not crash at this point; I could not pin down what loads the DLL again there.

### To Reproduce

1. Use Windows 11 build 26300 with dark mode on (applyDarkMode only runs for Theme Dark, or SystemDefault while the system is dark).
2. Download arrowloop-windows-amd64-portable.exe from https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/arrowloop/releases/tag/v2.2.8, or build the desktop/ module with node scripts/desktop.mjs.
3. Start it. The process exits when the first window opens.

### Expected behaviour

The window opens.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

Keeping a reference to uxtheme.dll for the life of the process avoids the crash: a package that calls windows.LoadLibrary("uxtheme.dll") in its init and never frees it, initialised before pkg/w32 (it sorts first by import path). With it the same build starts and runs normally. In Wails, dropping the FreeLibrary call in theme.go, or keeping the handle in a package variable, would fix it.

### System Details

```
Name              | Windows 10 Pro
Version           | 2009 (Build: 26300)
ID                | 26H2
Branding          | Windows 11 Pro
Platform          | windows
Architecture      | amd64
Go WebView2Loader | true

CGO_ENABLED       | 0

```

### Additional context

uxtheme.dll on this build has FileVersion 10.0.26100.8875.

items.title: [v3] OpenFile dialog with CanChooseDirectories(true) can't select files on Linux and Windows
items.body:
### Description

`OpenFileDialogStruct` carries `canChooseFiles` and `canChooseDirectories` as independent flags, but the Linux and Windows backends read only `canChooseDirectories`. When it is `true`, they open a folder chooser (`GTK_FILE_CHOOSER_ACTION_SELECT_FOLDER` / GtkFileDialog `select_folder`, and `cfd.NewSelectFolderDialog`) whatever `canChooseFiles` says.

`newOpenFileDialog` defaults `canChooseFiles` to `true`, so `OpenFile().CanChooseDirectories(true)` describes a dialog for files *or* directories. On macOS that is what you get, because `NSOpenPanel` takes both flags. On Linux and Windows you get a folder chooser where files can't be selected (greyed out under GTK, not listed on Windows). The "Open File/Directory" item in `v3/examples/dialogs` shows it.

Android and iOS already open a folder picker only when directories are all that is wanted (`canChooseDirectories && !canChooseFiles`).

### The trade-off, and the question

GTK and the Windows common item dialog have one mode or the other, so a dialog that accepts both kinds must pick one. Today, directories win. #6264 kept that on purpose for Windows multi-folder selection.

Changing it so files win, matching Android/iOS, would mean:

- **Fixed:** `OpenFile().CanChooseDirectories(true)` can select files on Linux and Windows, and folders stay navigable. Behaviour matches macOS more closely and the mobile backends exactly.
- **Changed for existing callers:** code that uses `CanChooseDirectories(true)` *without* `CanChooseFiles(false)` to get a folder picker would get a file chooser on Linux and Windows. The documented folder-picking pattern (#4793) already pairs it with `CanChooseFiles(false)` and is unaffected. The migration is that one call.

Is this a bug you'd accept a fix for, with the change noted in the changelog? Or would you rather keep "directories win" and document it? I have a small fix ready that moves the existing Android/iOS predicate onto `OpenFileDialogStruct` and uses it in all five backends, with tests, and can open it as a PR, or as a WEP if you consider it a change to public behaviour.

### To Reproduce

1. On Windows or Linux, run `v3/examples/dialogs` and choose "Open File/Directory" (or call `application.OpenFileDialog().CanChooseDirectories(true).PromptForSingleSelection()`).
2. A folder chooser opens, and no file can be selected.

### Expected behaviour

Either a dialog that can select files (as on macOS, Android and iOS), or documentation saying that on Linux and Windows `CanChooseDirectories(true)` always opens a directories-only chooser, whatever `CanChooseFiles` says.

### System Details

Built from source at master b6167d9b1. Found by reading the Linux and Windows backends; both code paths open the folder chooser whenever `canChooseDirectories` is set.

items.title: [v3] updater: a damaged or emptied staged payload installs over a working app, and the backup is discarded
items.body:
### Description

The updater verifies the download by digest while it streams, but that digest covers the **archive**, and `extract.go` deletes the archive as soon as it has unpacked it. Nothing checks the extracted tree after that.

The swap helper (`runHelperSwap`) stats the staged path once, before it waits for the parent to exit. `replaceTarget` then removes the installed application and renames the staged path over it. A `.app` bundle is a directory, and `os.Rename` of a directory succeeds whether or not anything is still in it. So a staged bundle that is emptied or truncated after extraction (during the parent's shutdown, or by anything else cleaning the temp directory) is installed. The helper logs success and deletes `App.app.bak`, and the user is left with an app that will not launch and no copy of the one that worked.

Nothing after the swap checks the installed bundle (its structure or its code signature) while the backup still exists. Once the helper reports success, there is no way back.

### To Reproduce

1. Build two versions of a v3 app as macOS `.app` bundles and publish the second as an update archive (any provider).
2. In the first version, call `Download` and wait for it to finish. The extracted bundle is staged at `$TMPDIR/wails-update-*/App.app`.
3. Damage the staged bundle before restarting, for example `rm -rf "$TMPDIR"/wails-update-*/App.app/Contents` or `: > "$TMPDIR"/wails-update-*/App.app/Contents/MacOS/App`.
4. Call `Restart`.

The same thing happens without step 3 whenever the staging directory is torn down while the helper waits for the parent to exit.

### Expected behaviour

The helper refuses a payload that cannot be an application, and leaves the original installed and relaunched. If the installed result fails validation after the swap, it restores the backup before discarding it.

### Actual behaviour

The damaged bundle replaces the working one. The helper log reports a successful swap, `App.app.bak` is removed, and the app no longer launches (step 3's first variant leaves an empty `App.app` directory).

### System Details

Found on master (b6167d9b1) by reading the helper and confirmed with unit tests driving `runHelperSwap` on macOS arm64 (in the accompanying PR). The end-to-end steps above have not been run as written. The Windows and Unix `replaceTarget` paths share the same sequence: stat once, then an irreversible remove and rename.

items.title: [v3] updater: a download during a pending Restart deletes the staged payload, installing an empty app
items.body:
### Description

`Updater.Restart` starts a detached helper that waits for the app to exit and then renames the staged payload over the installed application. After the helper is started, the updater keeps no claim on the staging directory. Two things can then go wrong while the app is shutting down.

**1. `DownloadAndInstall` during shutdown deletes what the helper is about to install.**
`DownloadAndInstall` starts with `discardStaging`, which runs `os.RemoveAll` on the staging directory, and that is the directory the waiting helper is about to install from. A staged macOS `.app` is a directory, and `os.RemoveAll` works depth-first, so the helper's path is left as an empty directory. `os.Rename` succeeds on it anyway. The helper reports success, discards the backup of the working app, and the user is left with an empty application and nothing to roll back to.

**2. A second `Restart` starts a second helper.**
`Restart` does not refuse a second call. The built-in update window runs `go u.Restart(ctx)` on every Restart click, so a double click starts two helpers against the same target.

### To Reproduce

1. `Init` the updater with a provider serving a zipped `.app`, then call `Check` followed by `DownloadAndInstall`. The update is staged and the state is `Ready`.
2. Call `Restart`. The helper starts and `Host.Quit` is dispatched.
3. While the app is still shutting down (an `OnShutdown` hook, a slow window close, or a periodic `CheckAndInstall` that fires in that window), call `DownloadAndInstall` again.
4. The staging directory is removed. After the app exits, the helper renames the emptied bundle over `/Applications/MyApp.app`, logs success and removes the backup. The relaunch fails because the bundle is empty.

For the double-Restart case: in the default update window, click "Restart" twice quickly. Two helper processes are started for the same target.

### Expected behaviour

Once a helper owns the staged payload, nothing in the running process should be able to delete it, and a second `Restart` should be refused rather than starting a second helper.

### System Details

Built from source at master b6167d9b1; macOS arm64. Found by code review and reproduced in unit tests with the package's own test seams.

items.title: docs: preserve v2 hosting, retire Crowdin and recover old links
items.body:
Preserve the current wails.io site while adding v2.wails.io, retire v2 Crowdin integration through final sync PR #5736, and add a v3 404 recovery page linking to v2 documentation without automatically redirecting visitors.

Review found #5736 changes 13 files: 11 translated credits pages revert newer accessible linked SVGs to an old contributor table; two French changes damage inline code and footnotes. All translated passages are already present on master. Preserve current content while retiring automation through the final PR.

Acceptance:
- Correct the final PR, preserving existing translations and credits; build before normal merge without bypassing protections.
- Stop automated Crowdin upload/import, remove build-time Crowdin API calls and active Crowdin invitations.
- Add v2.wails.io to existing hosting while retaining wails.io; verify HTTPS and representative locale/version routes. Do not switch the apex to v3.
- Add a branded accessible v3 404 with links to v2 and current v3 documentation, no automatic redirect; validate desktop/mobile and deep missing paths.
- Keep credentials and generated output out of commits.

User requests existing releases/v3.0.0 rather than new task branches. Cloudflare saved OAuth currently expired and refresh failed; requested restored access. Keep issue open until remote rollout is verified. Related: #5992.

items.title: [v3 docs] Clarify navigation and onboarding with Diataxis
items.body:
## Problem

The v3 reader-experience audit (#6338) found an approachable first-app path followed by competing Features/Guides/Concepts/Reference destinations, an unordered tutorial menu, and ambiguous CLI search results. Apply the Diátaxis user-needs framework to navigation and entry pages, while preserving existing routes and the current visual design.

## Scope

English documentation on `releases/v3.0.0` at `18a9809b3`. Use the published M-Press v1.0.20 for preview and validation. Do not move/delete pages, rewrite API examples, restructure translations, change the framework, or alter deployment.

- Keep the initial learning path explicit and provide a recommended Next Steps progression.
- Curate Tutorials in learning order and distinguish them from task-oriented how-to guides.
- Merge the competing Features and Guides navigation groups into one How-to Guides section, keeping topic groups approachable.
- Keep concept/explanation and API-reference destinations distinct; put options/method lookup pages with reference material.
- Reduce secondary top-level navigation and make migration/help discoverable.
- Give the two existing CLI reference pages distinct overview/detail roles and link them; retain all unique material and fragment anchors.
- Improve the task title for calling Go from JavaScript and verify search discovery.

## Acceptance

- Existing page URLs and heading anchors remain valid; no source page is deleted or added.
- No existing navigated route silently disappears; moved menu entries remain reachable.
- English onboarding/Next Steps/tutorial/reference entry points explain where to learn, accomplish a task, understand a concept, or look up facts.
- Strict build and link/asset checks pass with the released M-Press binary.
- Desktop/mobile screenshots and navigation/search task checks verify the rendered result.
- Record pre-existing translation gate failures separately; do not invent translations or claim a first-time-user usability study.

This is a documentation usability correction, outside the feature-only v3.1.0 milestone/project. Related accuracy work remains in #6337; this change does not attempt to adjudicate those API contracts.

items.title: [v3 docs] Restore usable article navigation on mobile and tablet
items.body:
## Problem

A reader-experience audit of the local `releases/v3.0.0` documentation at `18a9809b30ddd0303b1da22f4db12fc589e14ba6` found two related responsive navigation defects. This issue concerns usability, separate from the content-accuracy audit in #6337.

## Reproduction

1. Build with pinned M-Press 1.0.19 (`mpress build --strict --no-purge-css`) and serve `docs/mpress/site` as a static site.
2. Open `/quick-start/installation/` at a 390 × 844 CSS pixel viewport.
3. Click the apparent “On this page >” control. It does nothing: this is a `<strong>` element without a button role, keyboard focus, or disclosure behaviour. All `.toc > a` except `.active` have `display: none`, so there is no way to choose another section from the displayed table of contents.
4. Open the navigation menu. The fixed table-of-contents bar covers the top of the menu, including most of “Home”. At this viewport Home is at y=80..112 and the TOC spans y=58..100. `document.elementsFromPoint(50,96)` returns the TOC above Home.

The same active-only TOC pattern applies at the <=1050px breakpoint. The menu overlap was reproduced at 390px. Source: `docs/mpress/custom.css`, responsive TOC rules around lines 300–342. The menu starts at y=64 while the mobile header is 58px high.

## Reader impact

Readers on smaller screens lose the ability to jump through a long article and encounter an apparent control that cannot be operated. Opening site navigation leaves the article TOC on top of the menu. Desktop articles otherwise have useful full TOCs.

## Scope and acceptance criteria

- Provide an actual section chooser at mobile/tablet breakpoints, using a semantic disclosure/button or another keyboard-operable pattern.
- Show all applicable article sections when expanded and make selection scroll to the correct heading without hiding it behind fixed headers.
- Keep the article TOC behind/hidden while site navigation is open; Home must be fully visible and clickable.
- Verify 390×844, a tablet width within 721–1050px, desktop, keyboard focus, and light/dark themes.
- Keep existing navigation and desktop TOC behaviour working.

Severity: P2, documentation UI bug. Prioritise as a bug fix outside the feature-only v3.1.0 milestone/project. No implementation or push was performed by this audit.

## Wider assessment context

The onboarding sequence is clear and desktop pages are readable. Further improvements worth evaluating: simplify the many equally prominent sidebar categories; make Next Steps a guided progression; move the Windows Dev Drive optimisation tip below the first working-app milestone; and reduce search ambiguity. Current search reproductions: `CLI` returns two identical “CLI Reference” titles/descriptions (`/guides/cli/` and `/reference/cli/`, already related to #6337 consolidation); `call Go from JavaScript` places Method Bindings seventh, behind migration, a beta blog post, and contributor internals. `system tray` and `open file` return the expected feature first. These ranking and information-architecture recommendations are expert-review observations, not measured first-time-user study results.

Audit used a fresh local build and current screenshots in isolated Chromium at 1440×1000 and 390×844. Search Enter navigation, theme switching, platform-tab synchronisation, and the reading-settings panel were exercised. No production deployment, external search-engine discovery, screen reader, touch hardware, or network performance claims are made.

items.title: [v3.0.0][docs] Release-branch accuracy audit follow-up
items.body:
Release-branch audit completed against `3e03d19bdc5599c7eac71185f89c6e0596dec1de`. Corrections remain open. This issue is the authoritative follow-up tracker; the local report records audit evidence.

# Wails v3 release documentation audit

An audit of the checked-in v3 documentation found **31 actionable findings: 3 P1, 25 P2 and 3 P3**. The highest priorities are unsafe security examples and a misleading claim that binding directives prevent frontend access. The site builds and its links validate, but several documented examples and workflows do not match the implementation.

## Scope and baseline

- Audit date: 25 October 2026. Authoritative tracker: [Wails #6337](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/issues/6337), following the completed #5430 and #6086 accuracy passes. This report records evidence; follow-up work and status belong on GitHub.
- Audited source: `wailsapp/wails`, branch `releases/v3.0.0`, commit `3e03d19bdc5599c7eac71185f89c6e0596dec1de`; audit branch `codex/v3-release-docs-audit`.
- Source of truth: `docs/mpress/content/`, the v3 module, CLI parser, binding generator, runtime, standard templates, build assets and repository workflows. The Docusaurus website is the v2 site and was excluded.
- Inventory: 204 English pages, 52,259 English source lines, nine translated sets (1,827 translated pages; the new release-policy page has no locale copies), and the supporting contributor/build references. Historical blog posts and changelog entries were inventoried but were not treated as current API promises.
- The English page inventory and site were checked on this release branch. Identifier/source sweeps from the initial audit were reconciled with the changed release-branch files. Semantic review concentrated on onboarding, API references, binding generation, events/lifecycle, build/platform instructions, security, testing and contribution guidance. Streams, updater, mobile, menus, dialogs and environment material received targeted source checks, not exhaustive platform execution.
- This is an audit report, not a correction patch. Production documentation and implementation were left unchanged. Findings were verified against the release checkout and its code; the live-site deployment was not audited.

## Severity and evidence

P1 means copied guidance can compromise application security. P2 means a documented workflow, API contract or validation gate is materially wrong or blocked. P3 means a narrower inconsistency or misleading destination. Counts are distinct remediation items; repeated instances and translation diagnostics are not counted as separate defects.

Validation labels distinguish executed reproductions from source inspection. Native macOS/Windows UI, Linux distribution installs, code signing and mobile device workflows were not executed.

## Validation results

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| M-Press version | 1.0.19, matching the release contributor instructions |
| `mpress build --strict --no-purge-css` | Passed; 2,031 pages, 2,192 files |
| `mpress check` | Passed; no broken links or assets |
| `check_site.py docs/mpress/site` | Failed, nine missing release-policy language routes; all other checks passed |
| Documentation helper unit tests | Passed, 19 tests |
| `check_translations.py --mpress …` | Failed, nine missing translation files; 651 additional non-blocking warnings |
| Security examples | Reproduced nonce reuse and two directory-escape cases |
| Binding registry and server manager probe | Reproduced exposed annotated methods and contradictory return behaviour |
| Built CLI help and project generation | Reproduced invalid flag, signing command and source-file mismatches |
| Background panic | Reproduced process termination, exit status 2 |
| `sanity:gtk4` via Task dry-run | Reproduced missing-target error |

## Findings

### F01 P1 Encryption example reuses the GCM nonce

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/security.md:113`.

The example allocates a zero-filled nonce for every call and immediately passes it to `gcm.Seal`. It never fills the nonce with randomness. Executing the example twice with the same key and plaintext produced identical ciphertext and the nonce `000000000000000000000000`.

**Impact:** Applications copying this security example reuse a GCM nonce under the same key, compromising the security properties of authenticated encryption. This is a defect in the example; this audit does not establish that Wails itself uses this helper.

**Correction:** Replace it with a complete standard-library example using a fresh nonce from `crypto/rand`, or an appropriate random-nonce AEAD API. Explain the nonce prefix and matching decryption. [Go cipher reference](https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/cipher#NewGCM) documents the nonce requirement.

**Validation:** Executed standalone Go reproduction.

### F02 P1 File access example does not confine reads to the allowed directory

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/security.md:169`.

`strings.HasPrefix(absPath, allowedDir)` accepts a sibling directory sharing the prefix. The same code follows symlinks out of the allowed directory. A temporary fixture returned an outside file through both `allowed-outside/secret` and `allowed/link`, with no error.

**Impact:** Readers may expose files outside the intended directory through a bound method copied from the security guide.

**Correction:** Use a filesystem API that confines resolution beneath a root, such as `os.OpenRoot` and root-relative operations, and document supported Go versions. A lexical relative-path check alone does not address symlink escape.

**Validation:** Executed both sibling-prefix and symlink reproductions.

### F03 P1 Binding directives are presented as preventing frontend exposure

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/advanced.md:47`; `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/advanced.md:59`; `docs/mpress/content/contributing/architecture/bindings.md:88`.

`internal/generator/collect/service.go:239` makes `ignore` omit a generated method and makes `internal` suppress its JS export. The generated directives fixture still contains a callable `InternalMethod`. Runtime registration in `pkg/application/bindings.go:134` reflects exported Go methods and does not read source comments. A server-tagged probe registered both annotated methods and retrieved both by their fully qualified binding names.

**Impact:** A developer can mistake removal from the generated SDK for an access-control boundary and leave privileged exported methods callable.

**Correction:** Describe both directives as code-generation controls. State that exported methods remain registered in normal builds and that private operations must be unexported or moved off the bound service; enforce authorisation inside exposed operations. Qualify any separate obfuscation behaviour rather than promising universal hiding.

**Validation:** Executed binding registry probe with both directives.

### F04 P2 Typed event factories and signatures disagree with generated string constants

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/reference/frontend-runtime.md:130`; `docs/mpress/content/reference/frontend-runtime.md:161`; `docs/mpress/content/reference/frontend-runtime.md:225`.

The reference imports `UserUpdated`/`UserLogin` from `./bindings/events`, invokes them as factories, and describes `EventType<T>` overloads. This release branch **does generate** `events/index.ts`: `internal/generator/render/eventnames.go` and `eventnames.js.tmpl` export string constants. Consequently `Events.On(UserLogin, handler)` and the import path can be valid, but `UserUpdated(payload)` is not callable. The runtime uses `CustomEvents` augmentation and event-name strings.

**Impact:** Factory-style calls and documented overload signatures remain wrong; claiming that the events module is absent would itself be wrong on this release branch. Existing report [#5645](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/issues/5645) covers the original typed-event discovery problem.

**Correction:** Retain the generated constants and use `Events.Emit(UserUpdated, payload)`, or the string-literal equivalent. Document the runtime's actual name-based generics rather than EventType factories, and validate the example with this generator.

**Validation:** Compared release runtime signatures and generator templates; ran the release event-name renderer test and generated an events fixture.

### F05 P2 Typed events plugin example omits its required bindings path

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/reference/frontend-runtime.md:93`.

The reference configures `plugins: [wails()]`. `src/plugins/vite.ts:25` requires `bindingsRoot: string`, then resolves `${bindingsRoot}/github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/internal/eventcreate`. Without the argument it attempts a path starting with `undefined/`. The built-in Vanilla config correctly passes `wails("./bindings")`.

**Impact:** The documented plugin configuration fails type checking or event-module resolution.

**Correction:** Pass the bindings directory and explain that it is relative to the Vite project. Align with `guides/dev/frontend-frameworks.md:84` and the built-in template.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F06 P2 Time mappings contradict one another and omit the controlling option

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/models.md:319`; `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/models.md:468`; `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/models.md:710`; `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/methods.md:334`; `docs/mpress/content/concepts/bridge.md:131`.

The tables say `time.Time` becomes `any`; other sections promise `Date` and call `.getTime()`. `internal/flags/bindings.go:16` exposes `-time-type` with default `string`. The generated build task passes `-time-type=Date` for class/JS templates, but omits it for TypeScript interface templates. Committed fixtures demonstrate `Time: string` in the interface configuration and `Time: Date` with `DateFromTime` conversion in the class configuration.

**Impact:** Date methods fail for the default interface/string path. Switching generation modes silently changes the expected data shape if the reader follows these pages.

**Correction:** Document string versus Date explicitly, including `-time-type`, template defaults, JSON wire representation, and construction behaviour. Generate examples for both modes; do not replace every mapping with one universal type.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F07 P2 Model quick start reads a property excluded by its own JSON tag

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/models.md:21`; `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/models.md:42`.

The Go example declares `Name string` with `json:"name"`, then JavaScript reads `user.Name`. The later generated-model example on the same page uses `name` correctly.

**Impact:** The very first example returns `undefined` rather than the user name.

**Correction:** Read `user.name` and use one generated fixture to keep the Go definition and frontend property accesses aligned.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F08 P2 Counter service example does not compile

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/methods.md:100`.

The stateful counter declares `mu sync.Mutex`, then `GetCount` calls `RLock` and `RUnlock`, methods of `sync.RWMutex`, not `sync.Mutex`.

**Impact:** Copying this complete service fails compilation.

**Correction:** Use `sync.RWMutex`, as the services page already does, or use `Lock`/`Unlock` consistently.

**Validation:** Extracted the complete CounterService example and compiled it with Go; RLock and RUnlock were both rejected on sync.Mutex.

### F09 P2 Custom service names are said to allow multiple instances of one type

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/services.md:292`; `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/services.md:307`.

The listed use cases for `ServiceOptions.Name` include multiple instances of the same service type. `pkg/application/services.go:22` limits the name to logging/debugging. `Bindings.Add` rejects a duplicate fully qualified method regardless of that display name, explicitly saying to wrap additional instances in dedicated structs.

**Impact:** The suggested registration pattern fails rather than exposing two independently named service instances.

**Correction:** Remove that use case and demonstrate distinct wrapper types. Explain that `Name` does not change a binding namespace.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F10 P2 Window creation callback is incorrectly described as runtime ready

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/features/windows/events.md:52`.

`WindowManager.addAndRun` calls the OnCreate callbacks before `runOrDeferToAppRun`. Before `app.Run`, no window runtime has started. The page separately documents `WindowRuntimeReady` as the safe point for JavaScript.

**Impact:** Readers may emit events or call JavaScript too early and lose startup messages.

**Correction:** Describe OnCreate as a configuration/registration callback. Use `WindowRuntimeReady` for operations requiring the frontend runtime.

**Validation:** Traced the exact manager call order.

### F11 P2 Server mode reference gives incorrect return behaviour

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/server-build.md:202`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/server-build.md:212`.

The page says `NewWithOptions` warns and returns nil, and `app.Screen.GetPrimary()` returns an error. The shared manager creates a non-nil `WebviewWindow`; GetPrimary has signature `*Screen` and returns nil when there is no primary screen. A server-tagged probe observed `window nil=false` and `primary nil=true`.

**Impact:** Server adaptations based on the documented nil/error checks will be wrong; blindly dereferencing the screen can panic.

**Correction:** Separate native-host availability from Go window objects. Document exact Go signatures, nil behaviour, and the browser-side errors separately.

**Validation:** Executed a server-tagged manager probe.

### F12 P2 Build guides disagree about whether an ordinary build is debug or production

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/getting-started/your-first-app.md:83`; `docs/mpress/content/getting-started/your-first-app.md:112`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/cli.md:83`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/build/cross-platform.md:21`.

The first-app and CLI guide promise a debug executable and console logging from `wails3 build`. The cross-platform guide correctly calls it production by default. Current Linux/macOS/Windows build assets choose production flags unless `DEV=true` is supplied.

**Impact:** Users cannot follow the promised debugging workflow and may assume inspector/logging behaviour that was compiled out.

**Correction:** Document production as the generated default. Explain `wails3 dev` and any supported explicit DEV override separately, including platform inspector constraints.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F13 P2 Several build examples pass variables the generated tasks do not use

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/cli.md:98`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/cli.md:163`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/cli.md:213`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/build/customization.md:125`.

Examples use `PLATFORM=linux CONFIG=production` and `PLATFORM=windows ARCH=amd64`. The wrapper selects `GOOS`; the generated root task dispatches on `.GOOS`; platform tasks select development flags using `.DEV`. PLATFORM and CONFIG do not control the stock tasks.

**Impact:** A command can succeed while building the host platform or an unintended mode.

**Correction:** Use `GOOS=...` and the supported mode variable, and label invented variables as examples for custom Taskfiles rather than built-in controls.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F14 P2 macOS deployment promise disagrees with the generated build target

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/getting-started/installation.md:11`.

Installation advertises Intel deployment to 10.13 and Apple Silicon 11.0. `build_assets/darwin/Taskfile.yml:54` sets C flags, linker flags and `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` to 12.0. Some package-level Cgo directives still name 10.13, so even the source has multiple apparent minima.

**Impact:** The documented support promise does not describe binaries produced by the standard build workflow.

**Correction:** Establish one tested deployment contract, distinguish development-host requirements from binary runtime minimums, and align native and Docker builds. Do not infer a new framework-wide minimum solely from one flag.

**Validation:** Static build-setting contradiction; older macOS execution not tested.

### F15 P2 Linux missing-dependency remedy installs the legacy stack for the default build

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/build/linux.md:184`.

The guide correctly says GTK4/WebKitGTK 6.0 is the default, then its unqualified missing-WebKit remedy installs WebKit2GTK 4.1 runtime packages. Those packages match the legacy `gtk3` build, not the default stack.

**Impact:** A user with a default binary follows the troubleshooting instructions and still lacks its runtime library.

**Correction:** Provide separate GTK4/WebKitGTK 6.0 and legacy GTK3/WebKit2GTK 4.1 remedies, tied to the actual build tag and target distribution. Qualify AppImage portability claims by bundled/external runtime requirements.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F16 P2 Custom transport walkthrough omits a required interface method

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/custom-transport.md:43`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/custom-transport.md:73`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/custom-transport.md:120`.

The walkthrough implements Start and Stop and assigns `&MyCustomTransport{}` to Options.Transport. It never implements `JSClient() []byte`, although the reference later on the same page and `pkg/application/transport.go:18` both require it.

**Impact:** The walkthrough fails to compile before a reader can add their transport implementation.

**Correction:** Include JSClient in the first implementation and a complete request/response example. Clearly mark incomplete pseudocode such as `return resp` in the frontend skeleton.

**Validation:** Compiled the documented method set against application.Transport; Go rejected the assignment because JSClient was missing.

### F17 P2 End to end guide points a backend workflow at a frontend-only server

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/e2e-testing.md:33`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/e2e-testing.md:136`.

The guide uses Playwright against port 9245, the Vite UI preview. Wails native invocation is not provided by an ordinary browser tab there. The CI example starts neither Vite nor a Wails server and supplies no mocks or `webServer` configuration. `guides/build/customization.md:239` explicitly warns that bindings do not work at that browser-preview URL.

**Impact:** The claimed complete workflow has no backend connection locally and no running app in CI.

**Correction:** Choose and document a real harness: explicit mocks for UI-only tests, server-tag integration tests for bindings, or a supported native-webview automation path. Start and wait for that harness in CI; state which native capabilities it excludes.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F18 P2 End to end examples confuse browser upload and viewport APIs with native UI

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/e2e-testing.md:80`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/e2e-testing.md:100`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/e2e-testing.md:63`.

The save-dialog example handles a Playwright `filechooser` and calls `setFiles`, which is an HTML file-upload operation, not a native save dialog. The window test checks a newly created browser viewport without setting it to 800x600, not a Wails window. The delete test registers its browser dialog handler after the triggering click.

**Impact:** Tests either fail, dismiss the confirmation before handling it, or assert properties unrelated to the native behaviour they claim to validate.

**Correction:** Use uploads only for HTML inputs, register browser-dialog handlers before the action, and distinguish browser viewport assertions from native window checks. [Playwright upload documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/input#upload-files) and [dialog documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/dialogs) define the supported operations.

**Validation:** Compared examples with Playwright primary documentation; no GUI automation executed.

### F19 P2 Windows installer output is documented in the wrong directory

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/build/windows.md:22`; `docs/mpress/content/reference/cli.md:108`.

Windows packaging says the installer lands in `build/windows/nsis/<AppName>-installer.exe`; the CLI reference says packaged outputs land in bin. `build_assets/windows/nsis/project.nsi.tmpl:75` sets OutFile to `../../../bin/${INFO_PROJECTNAME}-${ARCH}-installer.exe`.

**Impact:** Users and CI scripts look in the wrong directory and omit the architecture in the expected filename.

**Correction:** Document the bin path and architecture-bearing filename; distinguish NSIS source files from installer output.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F20 P2 Setup guide points readers at the wrong defaults file

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/getting-started/setup.md:38`.

The page says `~/.config/wails/config.yaml`. `internal/defaults/defaults.go:112` returns `defaults.yaml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/wails`, falling back to `~/.config/wails`.

**Impact:** Users inspect or edit a file the setup wizard does not read.

**Correction:** Use defaults.yaml and describe the XDG override. Keep this distinct from per-project build/config.yml.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F21 P2 CLI reference invents a global flag spelling and scope

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/reference/cli.md:111`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/cli.md:660`.

The reference claims `--no-colour` works on all commands. `flags.Common` declares NoColour, exposed by clir as `-nocolour` on commands embedding Common. The audited binary rejects `init --no-colour`; accepts `init -nocolour --help`; and rejects even `version -nocolour`, because version does not embed Common.

**Impact:** Copying the global reference produces a flag error.

**Correction:** Document the parser spelling and actual per-command scope, or change the CLI deliberately and verify that all commands really inherit it.

**Validation:** Executed the built CLI help and rejected-flag cases.

### F22 P2 CLI reference denies a signing command that the binary exposes

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/reference/cli.md:71`.

The page explicitly says there is no `wails3 signing` command. The audited binary lists `signing` and `entitlements` at top level, and `wails3 signing --help` prints signing-specific flags. Conversely, `setup signing --help` prints setup help. This occurs despite the apparent nested construction in main.go.

**Impact:** The reference gives an absolute command-availability claim contradicted by the actual parser. Signing setup instructions need an executable check, not just inspection of builder calls.

**Correction:** Reconcile intended and actual command nesting, then document and test the chosen public path. Do not silently replace signing setup instructions based only on how NewSubCommand calls look.

**Validation:** Executed help only; no signing settings or credentials were changed.

### F23 P3 Template contributor guide mixes legacy metadata with the current layout

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/contributing/template-system.md:35`; `docs/mpress/content/contributing/template-system.md:172`; `docs/mpress/content/contributing/template-system.md:220`.

The guide says framework folders contain template.json, while later showing template.yaml and its TypeScript flag. It describes base as the Go layer every template starts from, but base contains frontend and NEXTSTEPS; normal template installation overlays _common and the selected template. The loader supports template.json as a legacy fallback, not the current generated format.

**Impact:** Contributors receive contradictory instructions on where metadata and backend boilerplate belong.

**Correction:** Make YAML the current authoring format, explicitly label the JSON fallback, and describe _common versus the base skeleton using the actual extraction path.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F24 P2 Release documentation is missing nine required translations

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/contributing/release-policy.md:1`; `docs/mpress/CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/mpress/scripts/check_translations.py`.

The release branch adds an English release-policy page, marked as a draft in its prose, without any of the nine locale copies. It has no build metadata excluding it from publication. The coverage checker reports nine missing translations. The site build includes the English route; its rendered-site validator requires corresponding translated routes. Stale segment findings are warnings unless --strict is supplied; missing translation files still fail the ordinary gate.

**Impact:** Warning-only stale auditing does not waive missing files. The release validation gate remains blocked by this specific page. The standalone M-Press build succeeds; `docs/mpress/scripts/build.sh` additionally runs the failing translation coverage check before invoking that build.

**Correction:** Translate the page when the owner approves its policy, or explicitly exclude an unpublished draft from both publication and coverage under one consistent rule. Do not silently accept missing published routes or treat draft policy as an approved release decision.

**Validation:** Ran the release coverage checker, which reports exactly nine missing files; rebuilt the site with M-Press 1.0.19. Full audit reports nine errors and 651 non-blocking warnings, with the same nine missing routes in the rendered-site check.

### F25 P2 Panic guide says a goroutine panic affects only that goroutine

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/panic-handling.md:15`.

The guide says only the panicking goroutine is affected. A standalone unrecovered goroutine panic terminates the process; the probe exited with status 2. Recovery must occur in that same goroutine. Wails recovery around particular dispatch paths is a separate behaviour.

**Impact:** Readers may assume a background worker crash is isolated and omit necessary recovery at its boundary.

**Correction:** Describe stack unwinding and process termination accurately, then identify precisely which Wails callbacks are recovered. Preserve the existing advice to handle background goroutines explicitly.

**Validation:** Executed standalone background-panic reproduction.

### F26 P3 Database guide links to a persistence example that the destination does not contain

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/patterns/database.md:15`.

The page promises that the TODO tutorial demonstrates SQLite persistence. The tutorial keeps an in-memory slice and instead recommends adding persistence as a future extension at lines 685 and 738.

**Impact:** The linked route exists, so link checks pass, but the promised worked example is absent.

**Correction:** Provide a real persistence example or link to a tutorial with actual persistence, describing its storage format accurately. Label the current database, REST, workflow, WML and Electron migration placeholders as incomplete in navigation.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F27 P2 Testing contributor reference names missing targets and overstates its test harness

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/contributing/testing-ci.md:88`; `docs/mpress/content/contributing/testing-ci.md:96`; `docs/mpress/content/contributing/testing-ci.md:117`; `docs/mpress/content/contributing/testing-ci.md:142`.

`sanity:gtk4` does not exist; the default sanity path and `sanity:gtk3` are present. The workflow table also claims Go 1.25, whereas the checked-in matrix uses Go 1.26 and 1.27. The page sends readers to TESTING.md for benign-race guidance and suppression rationale, which that cross-platform example-build guide does not contain. It describes build-and-launch checks where Taskfile example targets run go build. Its workflow summary describes the GTK4 variant as BUILD_TAGS=gtk4, while the workflow now installs GTK4 by default and uses BUILD_TAGS=gtk3 for the legacy variant.

**Impact:** Maintainers cannot run the promised command and may overestimate what a passing example build verifies.

**Correction:** Generate or check target names against the Taskfile, describe build checks separately from launch/runtime tests, and link race guidance only when it exists.

**Validation:** Executed the missing target with Task dry-run; inspected Taskfile and workflow.

### F28 P3 Runtime generation reference gives the wrong debug filename

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/reference/frontend-runtime.md:43`.

The page promises runtime.debug.js. `internal/commands/runtime.go:28` copies the debug source to a destination named runtime-debug.js.

**Impact:** A script or script tag based on the reference points at a nonexistent generated file.

**Correction:** Document runtime-debug.js for command output; distinguish it from the embedded source asset runtime.debug.js.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F29 P2 Window options reference contains the wrong callback type and default name

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/features/windows/options.md:59`; `docs/mpress/content/features/windows/options.md:87`.

The supposedly complete options structure declares KeyBindings as `map[string]func(window *WebviewWindow)`. The actual field is `map[string]func(window Window)` at webview_window_options.go:228. The Name description promises a UUID; NewWindow instead uses `window-<numeric ID>`. The displayed structure also omits options such as FullscreenButtonState and OpenInspectorOnStartup.

**Impact:** A callback copied from the type reference fails assignment, and the default identity contract is misstated.

**Correction:** Use the exact public field types and actual default. Generate the structure from source or label it as a selected-field summary.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F30 P2 Onboarding switches between TypeScript and JavaScript without changing templates

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/quick-start/first-app.md:30`; `docs/mpress/content/quick-start/first-app.md:126`; `docs/mpress/content/getting-started/your-first-app.md:30`; `docs/mpress/content/tutorials/02-todo-vanilla.md:181`; `docs/mpress/content/tutorials/03-notes-vanilla.md:32`.

The default is correctly described as TypeScript, but the next instructions tell the reader to open frontend/src/main.js. An actual `init -t vanilla` probe generated main.ts, not main.js. The generated index.html itself still names /src/main.js, so part of this is also a template defect, not merely stale prose. TODO/Notes assume JavaScript while selecting the default/vanilla template.

**Impact:** A new reader cannot open the named source file and may create a second entry point or encounter the template mismatch before reaching the lesson.

**Correction:** Choose one consistent lesson variant: explicitly select vanilla-js for JavaScript lessons or use TypeScript files and examples. Independently repair and verify the generated template entrypoint; changing only the prose does not fix that defect.

**Validation:** Executed CLI project generation into a temporary directory.

### F31 P2 Installation routes disagree about the required Go toolchain

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/getting-started/installation.md:25`; `docs/mpress/content/quick-start/installation.md:25`; `docs/mpress/content/status.md:24`.

The public release checkout has conflicting Go requirements: `getting-started/installation.md:25` says Go 1.24, while `quick-start/installation.md:25` and `status.md:24` say Go 1.25. The release `v3/go.mod:3` selects Go 1.26.0 and the common starter go.mod still declares 1.24. Go can select/download a newer toolchain automatically, so this is not proof that every installation using an older Go launcher fails immediately.

**Impact:** Users cannot tell which toolchain a release build selects or whether it requires an automatic download.

**Correction:** Align the stated effective build requirement with v3/go.mod, and distinguish the installed Go launcher from the selected toolchain and the starter module declaration.

**Validation:** Compared both installation routes, release status, v3/go.mod and the generated common module template.

## Structural recommendations

The main maintenance problem is duplicated reference material drifting independently. There are two installation/first-app routes, two CLI references, several event and menu references, and repeated Go-to-JavaScript mapping tables. The CLI still opens the older getting-started route. Consolidate factual reference contracts into one maintained source, and let tutorials link to those facts.

Under Diataxis, keep the first-app and QR/TODO/Notes pages as tutorials with one reproducible path and exact generated filenames. Keep field types, default values, CLI flags and conversion rules in reference pages derived from executable fixtures. Keep how-to guides such as custom transport, signing and end-to-end testing complete enough to achieve their stated outcome. Explanation pages can discuss alternatives without duplicating normative API tables.

Fix the three P1 items first, then the first-app/event/type examples and build contracts, then testing and contribution gates. Avoid a broad rewrite until examples can be regenerated and checked. For upstream triage, these corrections are bugs: prioritise by severity and keep fixes outside the feature-only v3.1.0 milestone/project, following the repository release policy. The findings are tracked in Wails #6337; no PR or push was made. Existing reports were searched before filing; the completed #5430/#6086 and typed-event #5645 context is retained.

## Reproduction evidence

Executed probes used temporary files and directories, the checked-in v3 module and Go 1.26.5. CLI probes were built with the server tag to avoid requiring a desktop display; native signing and packaging actions were not invoked.

```text
Repeated ciphertext: true; nonce: 000000000000000000000000
Sibling bypass: "outside allowed directory" error=<nil>
Symlink bypass: "outside allowed directory" error=<nil>
main.AuditService.InternalMethod registered=true
main.AuditService.IgnoredMethod registered=true
server NewWithOptions nil=false; primary screen nil=true
flag provided but not defined: -no-colour
flag provided but not defined: -nocolour  [version command]
wails signing - Configure code signing  [signing --help]
Task "sanity:gtk4" does not exist
panic: background panic; exit status 2
```

The binding probe used `application.NewBindings(nil, nil)`, added `application.NewService(&AuditService{})` after creating an App, and queried `Bindings.Get(&application.CallOptions{MethodName: name})` for both fully qualified method names. AuditService declared one exported method with each directive. The probe did not start a listening server or invoke privileged methods.

The release translation audit with M-Press 1.0.19 reports nine missing-file errors and 651 warnings: 252 missing-segment, 216 protected-content, 73 untranslated, 54 glossary, 36 structure, nine missing-file, nine invalid-target and two requirement-language findings. These are checker diagnostics, not 651 independently confirmed translation defects.

## Follow up boundaries

This report applies to the checked-in `releases/v3.0.0` baseline above. It makes no claim about the live website or a later branch tip. Native platform, device and signing workflows remain unexecuted where noted. The report contains evidence and suggested corrections; GitHub #6337 is the work tracker, and no documentation or implementation fixes are included in this commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- Correct or explicitly adjudicate each applicable finding against the release branch.
- Preserve generated event-name constants and correct factory-style usage (#5645).
- Replace unsafe copied examples and compile-check corrected examples.
- Reconcile release-policy translation coverage and the stated Go requirements.
- Run the pinned documentation checks and relevant executable examples; record platform limits.
- Keep bug fixes outside the feature-only v3.1.0 milestone/project and prioritise security guidance.

No documentation fixes, framework changes, PR, push or publication were performed by this audit. #5430 and #6086 remain completed historical passes.

## Local audit delivery

Commit `ddccb5688a1dbb118d6869a0209ba1fd2c7ea692` is on local `releases/v3.0.0` (fast-forwarded from `codex/v3-release-docs-audit`). Only `history/wails-v3-documentation-audit-2026-10-25.md` changed. Nothing pushed. CodeRabbit reviewed the report; both minor findings were addressed by clarifying the gate status and numbering the toolchain discrepancy (31 findings total). The required `coderabbit --plain` invocation is unsupported by CLI 0.7.6, so the supported `coderabbit review --uncommitted` was used. This issue stays open for remediation.

items.title: [v3 / linux] Dismissing a notification is reported as a click (DefaultActionIdentifier)
items.body:
**Version:** v3.0.0-beta.34 (also beta.32)

**What happens:** on Linux, closing a notification without clicking it (the close button, or dismissing it from the notification list) delivers a `NotificationResponse` with `ActionIdentifier: DefaultActionIdentifier`, exactly what a click delivers. An app that switches views or raises its window on a click therefore does that on a dismissal too, and it can't tell the two apart: the response has no reason field.

**Why:** `handleNotificationClosed` in `v3/pkg/services/notifications/notifications_linux.go` builds a default-action response whenever `NotificationClosed` arrives with reason 2 ("dismissed by the user"):

https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/v3.0.0-beta.34/v3/pkg/services/notifications/notifications_linux.go#L658-L676

Real clicks don't need that branch. `SendNotification` and `SendNotificationWithActions` always include a `default` action, so a click arrives as `ActionInvoked(id, "default")`, and `handleActionInvoked` removes the notification from the map. The `NotificationClosed` signal that follows a click then finds nothing and returns. The reason-2 branch fires only for notifications closed *without* an action, i.e. dismissals.

**Expected:** a dismissal sends no default-action response. Options:
- Drop the reason-2 branch.
- Or keep it only for servers that don't advertise the `actions` capability (`GetCapabilities`), where clicking may just close the notification.
- Or report the dismissal as its own response: a distinct `ActionIdentifier`, or a close-reason field.

**Repro:** send a notification with `SendNotification` on GNOME or KDE, register `OnNotificationResponse`, and close the notification with its X. The callback fires with `DefaultActionIdentifier`.

items.body:
### Description

In `wails dev` (v2.16.0), every page load in a plain browser at `http://localhost:34115` logs this in the terminal and the page console:

```
[Unhandled error] TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'nodes')
 > Fe ../../../wails/ipc.js:32:26544
 > bn ../../../wails/ipc.js:32:27002
 > new In ../../../wails/ipc.js:41:87
 > ../../../wails/ipc.js:41:367
```

The injected `/wails/ipc.js` has a `DOMContentLoaded` handler that mounts the "disconnected" spinner overlay with `new In({target: document.body, anchor: document.querySelector("#wails-spinner")})`. The bundled runtime is Svelte 5, which no longer supports the Svelte 3/4 `new Component()` API, so there is no active effect and the template helper fails reading `.nodes` of null. The overlay never shows; nothing else in the page is affected.

### To Reproduce

1. Run `wails dev` on a v2.16.0 project.
2. Open `http://localhost:34115` in Chrome.
3. Read the console or the `wails dev` terminal.

### Expected behaviour

No error; the overlay mounts with Svelte 5's `mount(Component, { target, anchor })`.

Wails v2.16.0, Windows 11, Chrome (WebView2 not involved: plain browser dev page).

[v3 beta.32] generate syso emits unreadable version resource on Windows
items.body:
## Description

`wails3 generate syso -info windows/info.json` produces a `.syso` whose
`VS_VERSION_INFO` block Windows ignores: Explorer / `FileVersionInfo` show
all-empty ProductName/FileDescription/CompanyName/ProductVersion — even with
the scaffold-default `info.json`. The icon and manifest halves of the same
`.syso` work fine (verified: our `.ico` art shows in Explorer), so only the
version resource is malformed.

## Evidence

- `.syso` (45,548 bytes) *contains* the UTF-16 strings (`ProductName`,
  `040904b0` translation, etc. — confirmed by grepping the binary), yet
  `[System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo]` reads everything empty.
- Reproduced with both the scaffold-default `info.json` (`My Company` /
  `My Product`) and custom values, so it's not input-specific.
- Control: the same metadata via `goversioninfo` (`versioninfo.json`,
  `0409/04B0`) linked into the same `go build` command displays correctly.
  So the toolchain links version resources fine — the generator's output
  structure must be off (length fields?).

## Repro

```
wails3 generate syso -arch amd64 -icon windows/icon.ico \
  -manifest windows/wails.exe.manifest -info windows/info.json \
  -out wails_windows_amd64.syso
go build -tags production -trimpath -buildvcs=false \
  -ldflags="-w -s -H windowsgui" -o app.exe .
# Right-click app.exe → Properties → Details: all blank
```

## Environment

- Wails `v3.0.0-beta.32` (CLI + module)
- Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (Build 26200), amd64
- Go `go1.27.2`, `CGO_ENABLED=0`

## Workaround used

Generate the `.syso` with `goversioninfo` (icon + manifest + versioninfo.json)
instead; only one `.syso` may exist at link time (`too many .rsrc sections`
otherwise).

items.title: [v3 beta.32] Native menubar panics on Windows (SetTextColor on garbage HDC)
items.body:
## Description

Attaching any application menu on Windows crashes the app during menubar drawing. `app.Menu.SetApplicationMenu(menu)` + window `UseApplicationMenu: true` → panic in the owner-draw path as soon as the menu bar paints (`WM_UAHDRAWMENUPOPUP`, `0x92`).

## Panic

```
panic: SetTextColor failed

goroutine 1 [running, locked to thread]:
github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/w32.SetTextColor(0xffffffff94011e00, 0xdedede)
        pkg/w32/gdi32.go:416
github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/w32.MenuBarWndProc(0x52129e, 0x92, 0x5?, 0x1001ff8e0, 0x22cc78a5cba0)
        pkg/w32/menubar.go:486
```

## Suspected cause

The HDC `0xffffffff94011e00` looks like a sign-extended 32-bit GDI handle: the low 32 bits (`0x94011e00`) are a plausible real HDC, the upper `0xffffffff` is garbage. That suggests wrong field offsets when reading `UAHDRAWMENUITEM`/`UAHMENU` for message `0x92` on this Windows build — i.e. the undocumented struct layout no longer matches, so `udmi.UM.Hdc` picks up a neighboring `-1` DWORD. `SetTextColor` then returns `CLR_INVALID` and the wrapper panics instead of returning an error.

## Repro

```go
menu := application.NewMenu()
file := menu.AddSubmenu("File")
file.Add("Quit").OnClick(func(*application.Context) {})
// ... any items
app.Menu.SetApplicationMenu(menu)
app.Window.NewWithOptions(application.WebviewWindowOptions{
    Title: "app", Width: 1280, Height: 800,
    URL: "/",
    UseApplicationMenu: true,
})
```

Menu contents don't matter — it crashes painting the top-level bar itself, before any popup content is involved.

## Environment

- Wails `v3.0.0-beta.32` (CLI + module)
- Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (Build 26200), amd64, NVIDIA RTX 3050
- WebView2 `155.0.4283.62` (`Go-WebView2Loader=true`)
- Go `go1.27.2`, `CGO_ENABLED=0`
- `wails3 doctor`: "Your system is ready for Wails development!"

## Notes

- Possibly related to the recent Windows menu fixes (#6103, #6104) — same code area, next bug over.
- Workaround on our side: don't attach the menu on Windows (`UseApplicationMenu` left `false`); macOS path unaffected.

items.title: v3 android: emulator tasks hit any connected adb device (false-positive boot wait + commands without -s)
items.body:
## Summary

The emulator-oriented tasks in the Android build assets (`ensure-emulator`, `run`, `deploy-emulator`, `logs`, `logs:all`) call `adb` without pinning a serial. When a physical device is connected alongside (or instead of) the emulator, two failure modes occur:

1. **`ensure-emulator` false success.** It runs `adb wait-for-device` and `adb shell getprop sys.boot_completed` unscoped, so *any* connected device answers — a plugged-in phone reports `sys.boot_completed=1` immediately and the task prints "Emulator booted successfully" even though no `emulator-*` serial ever appeared in `adb devices`.
2. **Unscoped install/launch/logcat.** With an emulator *and* a phone online, every bare `adb ...` invocation fails with `adb: more than one device/emulator`. With only the phone online, the install proceeds against the phone and fails `INSTALL_FAILED_NO_MATCHING_ABIS` (the APK contains only the host ABI, e.g. `lib/x86_64`).

## Reproduction

1. Connect a physical Android device with USB debugging enabled, no emulator running.
2. On an x86_64 host, from `v3/examples/mobile`: `wails3 task android:run`.
3. Observe: `ensure-emulator` reports success almost immediately (answered by the phone), then `adb install bin/<app>.apk` fails with `INSTALL_FAILED_NO_MATCHING_ABIS` (`adb devices` shows only the phone).
4. With an emulator running *and* the phone connected: the same tasks fail with `adb: more than one device/emulator`.

## Scope

- `v3/internal/commands/build_assets/android/Taskfile.yml` (canonical template embedded into projects)
- `v3/examples/mobile/build/android/Taskfile.yml` and `v3/examples/android/build/android/Taskfile.yml` (in-repo copies)
- Guardrail tests in `v3/internal/commands/android_taskfile_test.go`

## Acceptance criteria

- `ensure-emulator` resolves a running `emulator-*` serial (never satisfied by a physical device), waits — bounded — for that serial to register and then for that serial to report `sys.boot_completed=1` (existing 120 s budget), and exits non-zero with a clear message otherwise. No `adb wait-for-device` (unbounded, any-device).
- `run` and `deploy-emulator` install/launch exclusively via `adb -s <emulator serial>`; missing emulator → clear error, exit 1.
- `logs` / `logs:all` run against a pinned serial: emulator preferred, otherwise the first online physical device (preserves `run:device` workflows); clear error when nothing is connected.
- Physical-device tasks (`run:device`, `deploy-device`) unchanged — they already select a non-emulator serial and pass `-s`.
- `go test ./internal/commands/` passes; `wails3 task android:run` succeeds with a physical device plugged in.

items.title: [v3][Windows] Context menus open above the cursor (TPM_BOTTOMALIGN for all popup menus)
items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.30 (same code on `master`)

### Operating System

Windows

### Description

On Windows, every popup menu opens **above** the cursor, including webview context menus. `Win32Menu.ShowAt` in `v3/pkg/application/popupmenu_windows.go` always uses `TPM_LEFTALIGN | TPM_BOTTOMALIGN` (or `TPM_RIGHTALIGN | TPM_BOTTOMALIGN` near the right edge), with the comment "always position the menu above the cursor".

That fits system tray menus, because the taskbar is usually at the bottom of the screen. But the same `ShowAt` is used for window context menus (`menu_windows.go`). There, the menu covers the item the user right-clicked, which is not how context menus behave on Windows. Native apps (Explorer, Notepad, browsers) open the menu below and to the right of the cursor, and Windows flips it near screen edges by itself. On macOS, the same Wails app opens the menu below the cursor.

### To Reproduce

1. Register a context menu on an element (for example, a list row) in a Wails v3 app.
2. Run it on Windows and right-click the row in the middle of the window.
3. The menu opens with its bottom edge at the cursor and covers the row.

### Expected behaviour

Context menus open with their top-left corner at the cursor (`TPM_TOPALIGN`), like native Windows apps, and Windows repositions them near screen edges. Tray menus can keep opening above the cursor.

### Attempted Fixes

None in the app. The position is fixed inside `ShowAt`, so an app cannot change it. A possible fix: let `ShowAt` take the vertical alignment from the caller, with `TPM_TOPALIGN` for context menus and `TPM_BOTTOMALIGN` for the system tray. The manual right-edge check could then be left to Windows. I can send a PR if this direction is acceptable.

### System Details

Windows 11, 1920×1080 at 125% scaling, Wails v3.0.0-beta.30.

### Additional context

Found while testing a Wails v3 desktop app on Windows.

items.title: [v3] `-tags server` does not compile for GOOS=android or GOOS=ios
items.body:
## Description

Building `v3/pkg/application` with the `server` build tag fails to compile when `GOOS` is `android` or `ios`. The server-mode guide describes containers and headless Linux and never mentions mobile, nothing in CI builds this combination, and it has never compiled, so this is a report of an unsupported-but-not-rejected combination rather than a regression. The project should decide whether mobile server builds are meant to work and either make them compile or document/reject the combination.

## Reproduction

From `v3/pkg/application` on current `master` (`91a74c45e`):

```bash
CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=android GOARCH=arm64 go build -gcflags=-e -tags server ./
```

```bash
CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=ios GOARCH=arm64 go build -tags server ./
```

## Observed

Android fails with ten redeclarations between the `*_android.go` platform files and the server implementations, plus undefined bridge helpers because `application_android.go` and `application_android_nocgo.go` are tagged `!server` while the files that call into them are not:

```
./autostart_server.go:5:6: unsupportedAutostart redeclared in this block
	./autostart_android.go:5:6: other declaration of unsupportedAutostart
./autostart_server.go:7:6: newAutostartImpl redeclared in this block
	./autostart_android.go:7:6: other declaration of newAutostartImpl
./clipboard_android.go:11:6: newClipboardImpl redeclared in this block
	./application_server.go:356:6: other declaration of newClipboardImpl
./dialogs_android.go:41:6: newDialogImpl redeclared in this block
	./application_server.go:372:6: other declaration of newDialogImpl
./dialogs_android.go:111:6: newOpenFileDialogImpl redeclared in this block
./dialogs_android.go:168:6: newSaveFileDialogImpl redeclared in this block
./menu_android.go:13:6: newMenuImpl redeclared in this block
./single_instance_android.go:15:6: newPlatformLock redeclared in this block
./systemtray_android.go:30:6: newSystemTrayImpl redeclared in this block
./webview_window_android.go:16:6: newWindowImpl redeclared in this block
./clipboard_android.go:16:2: undefined: androidBridgeVoidString
./clipboard_android.go:21:9: undefined: androidBridgeString
./dialogs_android.go:72:2: undefined: androidBridgeVoidIntString
./webview_window_android.go:32:2: undefined: executeJavaScript
./webview_window_android.go:309:2: undefined: registerAndroidListener
./events_common_android.go:21:10: undefined: androidApp
./events_common_android.go:26:4: undefined: androidDebugLogf
./mainthread_android.go:9:10: undefined: androidApp
./mainthread_android.go:10:9: undefined: androidBridgeBool
```

iOS fails the same way, starting with:

```
./autostart_server.go:5:6: unsupportedAutostart redeclared in this block
	./autostart_ios.go:5:6: other declaration of unsupportedAutostart
./autostart_server.go:7:6: newAutostartImpl redeclared in this block
	./autostart_ios.go:7:6: other declaration of newAutostartImpl
```

## Constraint to be aware of

`TestSignalHandlerBuildVariants` (added in #6098) deliberately asserts that `signal_handler_android.go` and `signal_handler_ios.go` stay selected for `android`/`ios` builds **with** the `server` tag, keeping mobile lifecycle handling separate from the desktop signal handler. A blanket `!server` on every mobile file, as proposed in #6268, breaks that test. Any fix has to reconcile the two: either server mode on mobile keeps the mobile signal handler and the message-processor stubs while swapping only the GUI implementations, or the combination is explicitly rejected.

## Scope

- `v3/pkg/application` build tags for `*_android.go`, `*_ios.go`, `application_server.go`, `autostart_server.go`.
- Decision on whether `server` on a mobile `GOOS` is a supported target. If not, a build-time rejection (for example a `//go:build android && server` file containing a compile-time error with a clear message) and a note in `docs/mpress/content/guides/server-build.mpd`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Either both commands above compile, or they fail with a single clear message stating that server mode is not supported on mobile.
- `TestSignalHandlerBuildVariants` continues to pass without weakening its android/server and ios/server expectations.
- Desktop `-tags server` builds and non-server Android/iOS builds are unchanged.
- The server-build guide states the supported platforms.

## Related

- #6268 adds `!server` to the remaining Android files and is currently red on `TestSignalHandlerBuildVariants/android/server`.
- #5907 (closed) covered earlier mobile cross-compile build-tag failures.
- #6098 introduced the signal handler build-variant test.
