items.title: GTK4: frameless window resize jumps wildly — widget-local coords passed to gdk_toplevel_begin_resize which expects root coords
items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.28

### Operating System

Linux

### Description

On Linux with the GTK4 backend, resizing a frameless window from any corner/edge makes the window instantly jump and stretch (often beyond the screen). The resize gesture is completely unusable.
Environment:
- Wails v3.0.0-beta.28
- Linux, GTK4 backend (default build, no extra tags)
- WebviewWindowOptions: Frameless: true
- Observed on Wayland and X11

### To Reproduce

`handleButtonPressed` in `pkg/application/linux_cgo.go` (~line 1698) stores the
GtkGesture click callback's **widget-local coordinates** into the drag state:

```go
lw.drag.XRoot = int(x)   // x is GtkGesture "pressed" signal coord — RELATIVE to the widget
lw.drag.YRoot = int(y)
lw.drag.DragTime = uint32(C.GDK_CURRENT_TIME)
```

`startResize` then forwards these as the pointer position to
`gdk_toplevel_begin_resize`, whose `x`/`y` parameters are documented as the
pointer's **root (screen) coordinates**:

```go
C.beginWindowResize(w.gtkWindow(), edge, ..., C.double(w.drag.XRoot), C.double(w.drag.YRoot), ...)
```

The resulting geometry anchor is off by the window's own position, so the WM
resizes relative to a wrong pointer location — the window teleports/stretches.
`GDK_CURRENT_TIME` (0) as the timestamp is also suspect on Wayland.

Notably the GTK3 backend does this correctly
(`pkg/application/linux_cgo_gtk3.go` ~line 2044 uses the event's real
`event.x_root`/`event.y_root`), which is why `gtk3`-tagged builds resize fine.

### Expected behaviour

Translate the gesture coordinates to root coordinates before storing them
(e.g. `gdk_surface_translate_coordinates`, or query the pointer position from
the seat at event time), and use the gesture event's timestamp instead of
`GDK_CURRENT_TIME`.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

_No response_

items.title: [v3] Updater: GitHub provider fails to download assets from private repositories (uses browser_download_url)
items.body: ### Wails version family v3 ### Exact Wails version v3.0.0-beta.28 ### Operating System Windows ### Description The built-in GitHub Releases provider (`pkg/updater/providers/github`) always uses `browser_download_url` to download release assets. This works for **public** repositories, but fails for **private** repositories even when a valid Personal Access Token (PAT) with `Contents: Read` permission is supplied via `github.Config.Token`. For private repos, GitHub returns a body containing `Not Found` (HTTP 404) when requesting `browser_download_url`, regardless of the Authorization header. ### To Reproduce Reproduction Create a private repository and publish a release with at least one binary asset. Create a fine-grained PAT with Contents: Read + Metadata: Read on that repo. Configure the provider: ``` Gogh, err := github.New(github.Config{ Repository: "OWNER/PRIVATE-REPO", Token: "github_pat_…", }) ``` Call Check + Download (or CheckAndInstall). Manual curl confirmation: ``` # Listing works curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \ https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/PRIVATE-REPO/releases/latest # browser_download_url fails (body = "Not Found") curl -L -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -H "Accept: application/octet-stream" \ -o test.bin \ "https://github.com/OWNER/PRIVATE-REPO/releases/download/TAG/filename" # items.title: [v3] Custom protocol build/dev workflow loses Linux registration and needs end-to-end diagnostics
items.body:
Custom protocol support exists, but the standard build/dev workflow has gaps that obscure whether registration or delivery failed. This is a focused follow-up to #4026 and #4567, not a request to reimplement protocol support. The macOS single-instance capture fix (#5089) and GTK4 launch event fix (#6000) are already present in the audited checkout.

## Confirmed build pipeline defect

The protocol-aware `v3/internal/commands/updatable_build_assets/linux/desktop.tmpl` emits `%u` and `MimeType=x-scheme-handler/...`. However, `build_assets/linux/Taskfile.yml` runs `generate:dotdesktop` during native/Docker builds and packaging, overwriting that same output using `wails3 generate .desktop` with `-exec APP_NAME` and no MIME type. `dot_desktop.go` does not read config.yml or merge the old entry.

Reproduction:
1. Configure top-level `protocols: [{scheme: myapp, description: My App}]` in build/config.yml.
2. Run `wails3 task common:update:build-assets` and inspect build/linux/myapp.desktop.
3. Run `wails3 task linux:generate:dotdesktop` (also invoked by ordinary Linux builds).
4. Observe `Exec=myapp` and no `MimeType`, losing both association metadata and URL forwarding.

I executed the current Go desktop serializer in an isolated harness with the task's arguments: it produces exactly the above missing fields. The conflicting task/template paths were also checked against upstream. No desktop activation smoke test was performed.

## Other concrete findings

* NSIS `wails.associateCustomProtocols` quotes `%1` but not `$INSTDIR\${PRODUCT_EXECUTABLE}` in the command stored in the registry. Repro: generate an installer with a scheme and inspect shell/open/command after installing into a path containing spaces. Expected: both executable and URL separately quoted. This is source-confirmed; Windows launch behavior still needs a smoke test.
* Windows and both Linux backends detect startup URLs only when `len(os.Args)==2` and the argument contains `://`. A configured `myapp:payload` URL or `app --flag myapp://open` is not emitted as ApplicationLaunchedWithUrl. The second-instance callback receives raw Args instead of that event.
* `wails3 dev` has no protocol registration lifecycle on Linux/Windows. Linux/Windows run tasks launch only the binary. A user-local desktop entry/default MIME association or HKCU protocol registration could point to a stable development launcher. That launcher must preserve the dev server environment set by dev.go and handle links while the app is restarting.
* The distribution/custom-protocols guide's complete example parses the action from URL.Path, but `myapp://open/document?id=123` parses as Host=open, Path=/document. I reproduced this with Go net/url; the example dispatches document instead of open. Its manual Windows registration also omits the executable from the open command.
* The guide/example should demonstrate both ApplicationLaunchedWithUrl and OnSecondInstanceLaunch, sharing one handler, plus frontend readiness rather than assuming an application listener is already subscribed.

## Scope / acceptance criteria

- Preserve configured scheme MIME types and a URL placeholder through the actual Linux build/package task pipeline; add regression coverage for the task-to-generator integration.
- Quote the executable and URL separately in generated NSIS commands, with coverage for paths containing spaces.
- Define/document accepted URL syntax and CLI argument behavior; test it consistently across Windows/GTK3/GTK4.
- Provide an opt-in dev registration workflow for Linux and Windows with status/diagnostics and restoration of previous ownership; support rebuild gaps, dev environment, and separate dev/release identities. Avoid removing an association another app took over after registration.
- Document a shared cold-launch/second-instance handler and a frontend-ready pending URL pattern; correct the guide's parser and registry example.
- Exercise cold start, running instance, restart gap, spaces/escaping, and competing production installation in platform smoke tests.

Audit based on local checkout acc71e112. No implementation changes are included. Existing origin fork atterpac/wails has issues disabled, so this report is filed upstream. Suggested ordering: packaging correctness first, dev registration and unified delivery next.

items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.28

### Operating System

iOS (experimental)

### Description


Building with `wails3 task ios:run` on a machine that cannot upgrade beyond Xcode 14.2 fails with:

```
application_ios.m:192:24: error: property 'inspectable' not found on object of type 'WKWebView *'
```

The relevant code:

```objc
if (@available(iOS 16.4, *)) {
    vc.webView.inspectable = inspectorOn; // <-- compile error
}
```

**Root cause:** `@available` only guards runtime execution. The compiler still needs to resolve `inspectable` against the iOS SDK headers at **compile time**. Xcode 14.2 ships with an iOS SDK older than 16.4, so the symbol does not exist in the headers, and compilation fails before any runtime check is considered. This is consistent with reports from other projects using Xcode 14.2 with `WKWebView.inspectable`.

**Relevant context:** Apple’s documentation explicitly states that apps linked against an SDK before iOS 16.4 will not have the `inspectable` property available at compile time, and recommends conditional compilation guarded by SDK version macros for this scenario.


### To Reproduce

```bash
go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/cmd/wails3@latest
wails3 init -n mymob
cd mymob
wails3 task ios:run
```

### Expected behaviour

The project should compile successfully with Xcode 14.2 (iOS SDK < 16.4), or the documentation should clearly state that Xcode 14.3+ is required. Ideally, wails3 task ios:run should complete without errors on Xcode 14.2, using compile-time SDK guards so that WKWebView.inspectable is only referenced when the iOS 16.4 SDK is available.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

## 2. Suggested Conditional Compilation Fix

Replace the direct property access with a compile-time guard:

```objc
#if defined(__IPHONE_16_4) && __IPHONE_OS_VERSION_MAX_ALLOWED >= 160400
    if (@available(iOS 16.4, *)) {
        vc.webView.inspectable = inspectorOn;
    } else
#endif
    {
        @try { [vc.webView setValue:@(inspectorOn) forKey:@"inspectable"]; } @catch (__unused NSException *e) {}
    }
```
**How it works:**
- `__IPHONE_16_4` is only defined when compiling against the iOS 16.4 SDK (Xcode 14.3+).
- `__IPHONE_OS_VERSION_MAX_ALLOWED` reflects the SDK’s maximum supported iOS version.
- When using Xcode 14.2, the preprocessor skips the entire `if (@available(...))` block, so the compiler never sees `vc.webView.inspectable`. The KVC fallback (`setValue:forKey:`) still handles runtime behavior on iOS 16.4+ devices.

A simpler alternative that also works: remove the `@available` branch entirely and rely solely on the existing KVC path, since `@"inspectable"` is just a string key and requires no SDK declaration.

The documented requirements state Xcode 14.0 or later. However, the code as written effectively requires Xcode 14.3+ (iOS 16.4 SDK) to compile successfully.

Is supporting Xcode 14.0–14.2 an intended goal for the experimental iOS support, or should the documentation be updated to require Xcode 14.3+? If older Xcode versions are meant to be supported, I’d be happy to submit a PR with the conditional compilation fix above.

items.title: [v3][Windows] Tray icon disappears after sleep + lock + unlock

milestone.title: Future
milestone.description: Unscheduled feature work beyond GA. Placement here is not a commitment to a specific release. Goose should move items to a numbered milestone only when that release scope is justified.

items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

CLI:     v3.0.0-beta.27 Library: v3.0.0-beta.26 (from go.mod)

### Operating System

Windows

### Description

The tray icon disappears after hibernating for a while and then logging
back in. The icon is visible on the lock screen after wake, but vanishes
the moment the user session takes over.

Root cause: Windows registers tray icons per session. The icon rebuilt
on `Common.SystemDidWake` is registered while the session is still
locked, and the shell discards it when the user session takes over.
Wails reports the rebuild as successful even though `Shell_NotifyIcon`
was effectively ignored.

`v3/pkg/application/events_common_windows.go` maps only these power
events:

    events.Windows.APMSuspend:         events.Common.SystemWillSleep,
    events.Windows.APMResumeAutomatic: events.Common.SystemDidWake,

There is no mapping for `WTS_SESSION_UNLOCK`, and the message-only
window + `WTSRegisterSessionNotification` approach is not exposed by
Wails.

### To Reproduce

1. Start any Wails v3 app that creates a tray icon on Windows
2. Hibernate the machine (S4, not just sleep) for at least ~1 hour
3. Wake up. The tray icon is visible on the lock screen
4. Stay on the lock screen for a minute or two
5. Log in
6. Tray icon is gone. It does not come back on its own.

### Expected behaviour

The tray icon should remain present across the sleep→lock→unlock
cycle. Either Wails re-registers the icon automatically on
`WTS_SESSION_UNLOCK`, or it exposes an event the app can subscribe to.

### Screenshots
Debug log evidence (from my app, tracing the exact wake→login sequence):
[tray-debug.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33085006/tray-debug.log)

### Attempted Fixes

- Searched the issue tracker for "tray unlock", "tray icon disappear",
  "hibernate tray", "WTS_SESSION". Only #4153 (taskbar restart) is
  related, but covers a different scenario (explorer.exe restart, not
  session unlock).
- Read `v3/pkg/application/events_common_windows.go` and confirmed
  `WTS_SESSION_UNLOCK` is not mapped.
- Read `v3/pkg/application/systemtray_windows.go` and found the
  existing comment about `Shell_NotifyIcon` failures rolling back
  instead of re-registering.
- Worked around it in my own app: created a message-only window, called
  `WTSRegisterSessionNotification(hwnd, NOTIFY_FOR_THIS_SESSION)`, and
  rebuilt the tray icon on `WM_WTSSESSION_CHANGE` with
  `WTS_SESSION_UNLOCK`. This fixes the issue for my app.

Reference implementation:
https://github.com/SnishaperTeam/SniShaper/pull/135

### System Details

```shell
# System
Name              | Windows 10 IoT Enterprise LTSC 2024
Version           | 2009 (Build: 26100)
ID                | 24H2
Branding          | Windows 11 IoT 企业版 LTSC
Platform          | windows
Architecture      | amd64
Go WebView2Loader | true
WebView2 Version  | 154.0.4258.53
CPU               | Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4790K CPU @ 4.00GHz
GPU               | Intel(R) HD Graphics 4600 (Intel Corporation)
Memory            | 32GB

# Build Environment
Wails CLI      | v3.0.0-beta.27
Go Version     | go1.27.1
CGO_ENABLED    | 1
GOARCH         | amd64
GOOS           | windows
```

### Additional context

- The issue is reproducible every time when the machine hibernates
  for more than ~1 hour. Short sleeps (<30 min) do not trigger it,
  which is consistent with Windows rebuilding the shell session only
  after a long suspend.
- Tested on Wails v3.0.0-beta.26 library (beta.27 CLI).
- Workaround in my app for reference:
  https://github.com/SnishaperTeam/SniShaper/pull/135
  https://github.com/SnishaperTeam/SniShaper/pull/142
- Relevant Wails source files:
  - `v3/pkg/application/events_common_windows.go` (event mapping)
  - `v3/pkg/application/systemtray_windows.go` (icon lifecycle)
  - `v3/pkg/application/application_windows.go:305` (APMResumeAutomatic emit)

items.title: v3/linux: SetMenu with a newly created menu panics on an uninitialised native implementation

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
## Reproduction

On Wails v3 at `337a7571b`, with a running Linux window:

```go
menu := application.NewMenu()
menu.AddSubmenu("Probe").Add("Action")
window.SetMenu(menu)
```

The application exits through its fatal panic handler:

```
panic error: interface conversion: application.menuImpl is nil, not *application.linuxMenu
application.(*linuxWebviewWindow).setMenu
    v3/pkg/application/webview_window_linux.go:310
```

Reproduced with the existing GTK4 CGo backend on Fedora 44 under Xvfb. The purego backend reaches the same shared code, so this predates the migration. GTK3 shares this unchecked assertion as well.

## Cause and scope

`WebviewWindow.SetMenu` forwards a newly constructed menu to `linuxWebviewWindow.setMenu`, which assumes `menu.impl` already contains a native `*linuxMenu`. Public `NewMenu` leaves it nil. Calling `application.InvokeSync(menu.Update)` first avoids the panic, but callers should not have to know the native initialization sequence.

## Acceptance criteria

Passing a freshly constructed non-nil menu to a running Linux window initializes and attaches it on the GTK thread without panicking. Add coverage for both GTK variants and verify replacement/removal behavior. This is distinct from the GTK3 submenu-rebuild lifetime bug in #6231 and the Windows SetMenu issues #6102–#6104.

Severity: P1 (application crash). Bug fix for a nightly patch; keep outside the features-only v3.1.0 milestone/project.

items.title: v3/linux: rebuilding a GTK3 menu reuses destroyed native submenus

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
## Reproduction

On Wails v3 at `337a7571b`, after the application is running on Linux, create a menu with a submenu and call `application.InvokeSync(menu.Update)` twice:

```go
menu := application.NewMenu()
menu.AddSubmenu("Probe").Add("Action")
application.InvokeSync(menu.Update)
application.InvokeSync(menu.Update)
```

Build with `-tags gtk3`. The second rebuild emits `GTK_IS_CONTAINER`, `GTK_IS_MENU_SHELL`, and `GTK_IS_MENU` assertion failures, and leaves the submenu unusable.

Reproduced on Fedora 44, GTK 3.24.52, WebKit2GTK 2.52.5 under Xvfb. The existing CGo backend and the mechanically translated purego backend produce the same diagnostics. This predates the purego migration.

## Cause and scope

`menuClear` in `v3/pkg/application/linux_cgo_gtk3.go` removes native parent menu items. GTK destroys their owned submenus, but `Menu.impl` retains the submenu pointer. `processMenu` in `menu_linux_gtk3.go` subsequently tries to clear and populate that stale object. Related previous menu-rebuild work: #5464; legacy GTK3 tracker: #5465.

## Acceptance criteria

Repeated updates of nested GTK3 menus preserve live native submenu objects, reflect added/removed items, and emit no GTK critical warnings. Cover repeated rebuilds and menu teardown in a native regression test.

Severity: P2. Bug fix for a nightly patch; keep outside the features-only v3.1.0 milestone/project.

items.body:
Readiness rerun against master `3a83b2c65b76a89e3d47c33acd0cf5ddbe48df3b`, Node 20.20.2 / npm 10.8.2, 6 October 2026.

The setup wizard `npm ci` / build succeeds but `npm audit --json` reports **9 vulnerable package entries: 7 high, 1 moderate, 1 low**. A freshly initialized Vue TypeScript template builds but its installed dependency tree reports **3 moderate entries**. These counts include inherited findings across package chains; they are not counts of independent exploits.

`npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports **zero findings for both projects**. This is development/build-tool dependency maintenance; no exploit of the embedded wizard or packaged desktop app has been demonstrated.

## Reproduce

- In `v3/internal/setupwizard/frontend`: run `npm ci`, `npm audit --json`, and `npm audit --omit=dev --json`.
- Initialize and build the Vue TypeScript template, then run the same audits in its frontend directory.

## Audit paths

### wizard
- `baseline-browser-mapping`: moderate; https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w5vr-8v7q-w6rv
- `braces`: high; https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm
- `browserslist`: high; https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c83g-rgw3-j3cx, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-73wf-gq98-2v4g
- `chokidar`: high; inherited via braces
- `fast-glob`: high; inherited via micromatch
- `micromatch`: high; inherited via braces
- `nanoid`: high; https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8
- `postcss-selector-parser`: low; https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w9m9-85wc-3x92
- `tailwindcss`: high; inherited via chokidar, fast-glob, micromatch

### vue
- `@vue/language-core`: moderate; inherited via vue-template-compiler
- `vue-template-compiler`: moderate; https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g3ch-rx76-35fx
- `vue-tsc`: moderate; inherited via @vue/language-core

## Acceptance criteria

Update the relevant development dependency constraints/lockfile, or document an explicit, evidence-based exception for each remaining finding. Re-run clean install, audit, wizard TypeScript/Vite build, and a generated Vue build. Keep production-only audit at zero. Rebuild committed wizard assets when source dependencies affect them.

Existing dependency PR searches did not find a matching fix. #6095 updates docs/website lockfiles, so it does not cover these wizard/template paths. Avoid an automatic major Tailwind upgrade without validating wizard layout and embedded assets.

items.title: v3 setup wizard: changing signing identity retains the previous certificate Team ID

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
## Observed failure

On master `3a83b2c65b76a89e3d47c33acd0cf5ddbe48df3b`, macOS 26.4.1, run `wails3 setup` with an isolated, empty `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and two installed certificates belonging to different teams.

The signing step automatically selects an Apple Development identity and fills its Team ID (team A). Selecting a Developer ID Application identity belonging to team B changes the identity but leaves the Team ID field set to team A. Proceeding through setup saves that mismatched pair in defaults.yaml.

In this run, signing a universal bundle using the saved identity succeeded, and `codesign -dv` reported the actual certificate's team B. The saved Team ID was still team A. No notarization request was submitted; an Apple rejection is not claimed.

## Reproduction

1. Open setup with clean isolated settings and certificates from two teams.
2. Let the signing step choose the first identity and extract its team.
3. Choose another identity with a different parenthesized Team ID.
4. Observe that the Team ID field retains the first value.
5. Finish setup and inspect the saved identity/team pair.

## Code path

`internal/setupwizard/frontend/src/components/SigningStep.tsx` uses `config.darwin?.teamID || extractTeamID(identity)` for identity changes (including the dropdown). A previous automatically populated Team ID is nonempty, so it prevents updating to the new identity's team. The notarization setup receives that stale Team ID.

## Acceptance criteria

Automatically derived Team IDs must follow identity selection changes. If a manually overridden Team ID is intentionally preserved, clearly distinguish it from an automatically derived value and validate/show the mismatch. Saved settings and notarization profile creation must use a coherent identity/team pair. Cover switching identities from different teams.

items.title: v3 ios template: macOS dev window is blank with IPv6-only Vite localhost listener

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
## Observed failure

Readiness rerun on master `3a83b2c65b76a89e3d47c33acd0cf5ddbe48df3b`, macOS 26.4.1 arm64 / Node 20.20.2, using the `ios` bundled template as a macOS desktop app.

`wails3 dev` compiles and launches, and logs `Connected to frontend dev server!`, but its native window is blank. The following native asset request fails:

```
[ExternalAssetHandler] Proxy error error=dial tcp4 127.0.0.1:9250: connect: connection refused
```

The template has no Vite config and its dev script is just `vite`. `lsof` showed Node listening on `[::1]:9250` only. The frontend loads and live reloads at `http://localhost:9250` in a browser, while `http://127.0.0.1:9250` refuses the connection. `internal/assetserver/build_dev.go` forces `tcp4` for localhost proxy connections. This explains why the frontend health check succeeds but the native asset proxy cannot reach it.

## Reproduce

1. Build the CLI from this master.
2. `wails3 init -n ipv6-repro -t ios` in an unsynced directory.
3. Point the generated Go module at the same local Wails checkout.
4. `wails3 dev -port 9250` on a Mac where localhost/Vite selects IPv6.
5. Observe the blank native window, proxy error, and IPv6-only Vite listener.

Go file changes still restarted the app process; this is specifically a frontend transport/rendering failure. Other Vite templates bound IPv4 and loaded normally in this run. The earlier closed #5348 is related localhost/proxy history, but this report covers the current ios template on master.

## Acceptance criteria

The unmodified ios template must render in the native macOS dev window when localhost resolves to IPv6, and frontend reload and Go restart must continue to work. Coordinate Vite binding and the asset proxy without regressing Windows localhost handling. This blocks the all-template GA dev gate.

milestone.title: Future

items.body:
## Environment - Wails v3.0.0-beta.27 — the macOS zoom code is unchanged since v3's first commit (`81645190f0`, 2023-01), so every beta behaves the same; also reproduced on `master` at 3a83b2c65b (2026-10-05) - macOS 27.0 (26A428), darwin/arm64, Go 1.27.1 ## Description On macOS `Window.ZoomIn()`, `ZoomOut()`, `ZoomReset()`, `SetZoom()` and `GetZoom()` — and with them the `ZoomIn` / `ZoomOut` / `ResetZoom` menu roles, i.e. ⌘+ / ⌘− / ⌘0 in the View menu that `NewViewMenu()` builds — are implemented with `-[WKWebView setMagnification:]` (`windowZoomIn` & co. in `v3/pkg/application/webview_window_darwin.go`). `magnification` is a view-level scale transform, the pinch-to-zoom kind: the page keeps its layout viewport, is drawn larger, and whatever no longer fits is cut off at the right and bottom edges (it can be scrolled into view). Nothing reflows — text keeps its line breaks, responsive layouts keep their breakpoints, elements anchored to the right edge leave the window. The other two backends implement the same API as a *browser zoom*: Windows through `ICoreWebView2Controller::put_ZoomFactor`, Linux through `webkit_web_view_set_zoom_level`. There the CSS viewport shrinks, text wraps and the layout adapts — what ⌘+ does in Safari, Chrome, Edge or any Electron app, and what users expect from the shortcut. macOS is the odd one out. WKWebView has had the browser-zoom equivalent since macOS 11: [`pageZoom`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/webkit/wkwebview/pagezoom). It is what Safari's View → Zoom In drives, and it leaves `magnification` to the pinch gesture (`AllowsMagnification`). ## To Reproduce Interactively: any app with the default View menu and a page of wrapping text — press ⌘+ a few times. The right part of the page disappears and a horizontal scrollbar shows up instead of the text re-wrapping. Programmatically — an 800 px window with a long paragraph; 1.5 s after start Go calls `ZoomIn()` six times (→ 1.30), then `ZoomReset()`, and after each step the page reports its viewport metrics back through the asset handler: `main.go` ```go package main import ( _ "embed" "fmt" "net/http" "os" "time" "github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application" ) //go:embed index.html var index []byte func main() { mux := http.NewServeMux() mux.HandleFunc("/", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/html") w.Write(index) }) mux.HandleFunc("/report", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { fmt.Println("page:", r.URL.RawQuery) }) app := application.New(application.Options{ Name: "zoomrepro", Assets: application.AssetOptions{Handler: mux}, }) window := app.Window.NewWithOptions(application.WebviewWindowOptions{URL: "/", Width: 800, Height: 500}) go func() { time.Sleep(1500 * time.Millisecond) report(window, "initial") for i := 0; i < 6; i++ { window.ZoomIn() } time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond) fmt.Printf("GetZoom=%.2f\n", window.GetZoom()) report(window, "zoomed") window.ZoomReset() time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond) report(window, "reset") time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond) app.Quit() }() if err := app.Run(); err != nil { fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err) os.Exit(1) } } func report(window *application.WebviewWindow, tag string) { window.ExecJS(fmt.Sprintf(`fetch('/report?' + new URLSearchParams({ tag: %q, innerWidth: innerWidth, clientWidth: document.documentElement.clientWidth, vvWidth: Math.round(visualViewport.width), vvScale: visualViewport.scale.toFixed(2), lines: document.getElementById('p').getClientRects().length, rightEdge: Math.round(document.getElementById('r').getBoundingClientRect().right), }))`, tag)) time.Sleep(400 * time.Millisecond) } ``` `index.html` (the runtime is loaded only because `ExecJS` is queued until it is) ```html

items.title: v3 macOS: repeat package and dev restart fail signing bundles in file-provider-backed folders

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
## Problem

On macOS, a Wails v3 project in a file-provider-backed Documents folder packages successfully once, then `wails3 package` fails on the next run at `codesign --force --deep --sign -` with:

```
resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed
```

The same problem prevents the second `wails3 dev` run after a Go source change from restarting its `.dev.app`. `wails3 tool sign` can also report success on this bundle while a subsequent `codesign --verify --deep --strict` fails, because Finder metadata is attached again.

## Reproduction (2026-10-05 master `aab280f2880bc6569f0773af84496c643364436c`)

Host: macOS 26.4.1, arm64, Xcode 26.6, Go 1.26.2. Generate a vanilla or React project under a file-provider-backed `~/Documents` folder.

1. Build the CLI from `v3/cmd/wails3`.
2. `wails3 init -n ReadyReact -t react -d <Documents-folder>`.
3. `cd <Documents-folder>/ReadyReact && wails3 package` — succeeds and creates an ad-hoc signed `.app`.
4. Run `wails3 package` again — fails at `darwin:codesign:adhoc` with the message above.
5. `xattr -lr bin/readyreact.app` shows `com.apple.FinderInfo`, `com.apple.fileprovider.fpfs#P`, and `com.apple.provenance` on the bundle. The failing CLI output is `bin/readyreact.app: replacing existing signature` followed by the error.

With `wails3 dev` in the same folder, editing `main.go` triggers a successful Go rebuild, but `darwin:run` fails while re-signing the existing `.dev.app`; the watcher exits instead of restarting the app.

**Control:** The same CLI and master source generated a React JavaScript project in `/private/tmp`. Two successive `wails3 package` runs both succeeded and `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passed. A vanilla project there restarted successfully after a Go edit with a new app PID. Direct Developer ID signing of a clean bundle in `/private/tmp` also passed strict verification.

## Expected

Repeated packaging and Go-triggered dev restarts work from common macOS project locations, including file-provider-backed Documents folders. Signing either succeeds with a bundle that passes strict verification or reports the failure clearly.

## Acceptance criteria

- Repeated `wails3 package` on the same macOS project succeeds in a file-provider-backed folder.
- A Go edit during `wails3 dev` restarts the macOS app in that folder.
- Both ad-hoc and Developer ID signed bundles pass `codesign --verify --deep --strict` after the command completes.
- Add a regression check for disallowed bundle extended attributes before re-signing, or document an equivalent robust handling path.

items.body:
### Wails version family v3 ### Exact Wails version v3.0.0-beta.27 ### Operating System Windows ### Description After upgrading a Windows application from Wails v3.0.0-alpha2.117 to v3.0.0-beta.27, the native window appears promptly but its content stays blank noticeably longer. The example imports 24 tiny local ES modules in parallel, then inserts a heading and two paragraphs into the DOM. Each module handler immediately returns a single export statement. On my machine, production builds gave the following FCP timings. Each version has 8 measured launches after one warm-up; execution order alternates between versions. | Version | Median | Range | Launches above 1 second | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | alpha2.117 | 602.9 ms | 582.8–674.0 ms | 0/8 | | beta.27 | 2102.1 ms | 592.6–2676.3 ms | 7/8 | In all 8 beta samples, the DOM insertion finished 96.3–108.6 ms after navigation began. In the slow samples, FCP followed about 1–2 seconds later. No JavaScript long tasks (>50 ms), error events, or unhandled rejections were captured. items.title: [macOS] ExecJS over-releases its NSString when the runtime is called from the main thread (crash in block dispose helper)
items.body:
### Description

On macOS, `ExecJS` in `v2/internal/frontend/desktop/darwin/Application.m` over-releases the script string. The crash only shows up when the Wails runtime is entered from the AppKit main thread (for example `runtime.EventsEmit` or `runtime.WindowShow` called synchronously from a system-tray click callback), which is why ordinary bindings and goroutines never hit it.

```objc
void ExecJS(void* inctx, const char *script) {
    WailsContext *ctx = (__bridge WailsContext*) inctx;
    NSString *nsscript = safeInit(script);      // stringWithUTF8String: → autoreleased
    ON_MAIN_THREAD(
       [ctx ExecJS:nsscript];
       [nsscript release];                      // explicit release…
    );                                          // …and the block's dispose helper releases it again
}
```

`safeInit` returns an autoreleased string. `dispatch_async` copies the block, which retains the captured `nsscript`; the block body releases it; the block's dispose helper (`__destroy_helper_block_e8_32o40o`) releases it once more. That is one release too many relative to the retains. It balances by accident when the caller is a Go-created thread, because those threads have no autorelease pool and the pending autorelease never fires. When the caller is the main thread, AppKit's pool drains between the dispatch and the block running, so the dispose helper calls `objc_release` on freed memory.

Still present on `master` as of today.

### To Reproduce

1. `wails init -t react-ts`, add `fyne.io/systray` (or any code that calls back into Go on the AppKit main thread).
2. In `OnStartup`, register a tap handler that calls `runtime.EventsEmit(ctx, "x", nil)` synchronously inside the callback.
3. Build, run, click the status item with the mouse.

Expected: the event reaches the frontend. Actual: `SIGSEGV … signal arrived during cgo execution` on the main thread.

Moving the `EventsEmit` call onto a goroutine (`go func() { runtime.EventsEmit(...) }()`) makes the crash disappear, which confirms the thread dependence.

### Trace

lldb (debug build, Go's signal handler bypassed):

```
* thread #1, queue = 'com.apple.main-thread', stop reason = EXC_BAD_ACCESS (code=1, address=0x39540d115790)
  * frame #0: libobjc.A.dylib`objc_release + 16
    frame #1: app`__destroy_helper_block_e8_32o40o + 40
    frame #2: libsystem_blocks.dylib`_call_dispose_helpers_excp + 48
    frame #3: libsystem_blocks.dylib`_Block_release + 236
    frame #4: libdispatch.dylib`_dispatch_client_callout + 16
    frame #5: libdispatch.dylib`_dispatch_main_queue_drain.cold.6 + 832
    frame #6: libdispatch.dylib`_dispatch_main_queue_drain + 176
    frame #7: libdispatch.dylib`_dispatch_main_queue_callback_4CF + 44
    frame #8: CoreFoundation`__CFRUNLOOP_IS_SERVICING_THE_MAIN_DISPATCH_QUEUE__ + 16
    ...
    frame #18: AppKit`-[NSApplication run] + 368
    frame #19: app`RunMainLoop + 40
    frame #20: app`_cgo_..._Cfunc_RunMainLoop + 20
```

`nm` on the binary places `__destroy_helper_block_e8_32o40o` immediately after `___ExecJS_block_invoke` and `___copy_helper_block_e8_32o40o`, i.e. it is the ExecJS block's helper.

### Suggested fix

Either drop the explicit `[nsscript release]` inside the block (the block copy/dispose pair already balances the autoreleased string), or have `safeInit` return an owned string (`[[NSString alloc] initWithUTF8String:]`) and keep the explicit release while making sure it is not released twice. The same pattern (`safeInit` + explicit release inside `ON_MAIN_THREAD`) appears in several other functions in `Application.m` (`SetTitle`, `SetBackgroundColour`, …) and is worth auditing together.

### Environment

- Wails v2.15.0 (also reproducible against `master` `Application.m`)
- macOS 26 (Darwin 25.5.0), Apple Silicon
- Go 1.27.0
- `wails doctor`: no issues reported

items.title: Windows: default info.json language key "0000" produces a VERSIONINFO resource Explorer cannot display (file properties show empty version)
items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.27

### Operating System

Windows

### Description

The default `build/windows/info.json` produced by `wails3 init` uses `"0000"` (LCID 0) as the key of the `info` map. `wails3 generate syso -info windows/info.json` parses those keys as LANGIDs (`version.Info.UnmarshalJSON` reads them with `%X` into a uint16 lang table) and embeds the VERSIONINFO resource accordingly.

The resource bytes end up in the exe (the strings are visible as UTF-16 data), but the Windows VersionInfo API returns empty strings for it:

- Explorer "Properties -> Details" shows no File version / Product version / Product name
- PowerShell `(Get-Item .\app.exe).VersionInfo.FileVersion` is empty

Renaming the key to `"0409"` (en-US) fixes it immediately: the same build then displays FileVersion 0.1.0, ProductVersion 0.1.0 and the product name correctly.

Note: `"040904b0"`-style keys overflow the uint16 langID parameter and do not work, so the fix is specifically a plain LANGID like `0409`.

Since the default template produces a version resource the shell cannot read, every project created from the template silently ends up with empty file-properties version details.

### To Reproduce

1. wails3 init (default template; keep build/windows/info.json with "info": { "0000": { ... } })
2. wails3 generate syso -arch amd64 -icon build/windows/icon.ico -manifest build/windows/wails.exe.manifest -info build/windows/info.json -out wails_windows_amd64.syso
3. go build (windowsgui) and open the exe Properties -> Details: File version / Product version are empty
4. Edit build/windows/info.json: rename "0000" to "0409", regenerate the syso, rebuild
5. Properties -> Details now shows FileVersion/ProductVersion/ProductName correctly

Control experiment isolating the bug to the template/mapping (not the winres library):
- `go run github.com/tc-hib/go-winres@v0.3.1 simply --arch amd64 --product-version 0.1.0 ...` produces a syso whose version info Explorer displays correctly with the same winres version

### Expected behaviour

The default template's info.json should produce a version resource the Windows shell can display (either ship a displayable LANGID like "0409" in the template, or have the syso generator map LCID 0 to a valid language/codepage for the string table).

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

1. Renamed the info.json language key "0000" -> "0409": fixes it (verified FileVersion/ProductVersion display)
2. Tried "040904b0": does not work (overflows the uint16 langID in winres Set)
3. Verified against go-winres v0.3.1 (same winres library) generating the resource directly: works, so the library is fine and the template key / mapping is the problem
4. Web searched the v3 changelog and issue tracker: no existing report found

### System Details

```shell
# System
Name              | Windows 10 Pro (Windows 11 Pro)
Version           | 2009 (Build: 26200) / ID 25H2
Platform          | windows
Architecture      | amd64
Go WebView2Loader | true
WebView2 Version  | 154.0.4258.48
CPU               | 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12600K
Memory            | 48GB

# Build Environment
Wails CLI  | v3.0.0-beta.27
Go Version | go1.25.14
-buildmode | exe
-compiler  | gc
```

### Additional context

- The VERSIONINFO strings ARE embedded in the exe (visible as UTF-16 bytes), but the Windows VersionInfo API returns empty strings - the resource layout produced from LCID 0 is what the shell cannot parse.
- Our app worked around this locally by renaming the key to "0409"; the report is about the default template so future projects don't hit it.
- Our repro project is private, but the steps above use only the default `wails3 init` template output plus the listed commands - happy to provide more details if needed.

items.title: [v3] dev readiness check never passes against Vite (no Accept header → 404)

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.27

### Operating System

Windows

### Description

Since #6150 (v3.0.0-beta.26), `wails3 dev` adds an HTTP readiness check to the standard
`wails3 task common:dev:frontend` background step. Holding the primary back until the frontend is
reachable is intended, and that part works as designed.

The check itself never succeeds against a Vite dev server. It requests `FRONTEND_DEVSERVER_URL`
with a bare `http.Client`, which sends **no `Accept` header**. Vite answers a `GET /` without
`Accept` with **404**, while the probe requires exactly **HTTP 200**. The gate therefore blocks
`wails3 task run` for its entire 60s budget and only reports the failure at timeout — so the
symptom is a one-minute hang followed by an error, not a "the frontend is down" message.

Observed on Windows ( first on `v3.0.0-beta.26`, still present on `v3.0.0-beta.27` ):

```
ERROR   starting processes: process "wails3 task common:dev:frontend" did not become ready
on http://localhost:9245 within 1m0s: context deadline exceeded
```

Minimal repro is a stock `wails3 init` project — no project-specific configuration is involved.

### To Reproduce

1. Use any Wails v3 project with a Vite frontend and the default `build/config.yml` `dev_mode`
   block (i.e. `wails3 task common:dev:frontend` as a `background` step, with no explicit
   `readiness` on it).
2. Run `wails3 dev`.
3. Vite starts and is serving correctly:

   ```
   VITE v3.2.11  ready in 474 ms
   ➜  Local:   http://127.0.0.1:9245/
   ```

4. After ~60 seconds:

   ```
   ERROR   starting processes: process "wails3 task common:dev:frontend" did not become ready
   on http://localhost:9245 within 1m0s: context deadline exceeded
   ```

5. The primary process is never launched, and wails3 exit.

Directly showing the mismatch — **same Vite server, same address, only the request headers differ**:

```
default Go http.Client (no Accept)   -> HTTP 404
+ Accept: */*                        -> HTTP 200 (index.html)
+ Accept: text/html                  -> HTTP 200
curl (Accept stripped)               -> HTTP 404
curl (Accept: */*)                   -> HTTP 200
```

### Expected behaviour

The probe should receive HTTP 200 from the healthy frontend dev server within milliseconds and the
primary should start normally. `FRONTEND_DEVSERVER_URL` points at a server that happily returns
`index.html` for `/` to a browser, so the readiness check should not depend on a header that every
browser sends but Go's default client does not.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

* Searched the issue tracker and discussions for "did not become ready", readiness, and dev-server
  readiness. The nearest matches are unrelated: #6048 (dev teardown), #4905 (connecting to an
  already-running frontend), #4556 (proxy dial to `[::1]`), #4620 (Vite 7.1.8).
* Ruled out an IP/host mismatch, which was the obvious first suspicion:
  * `http://localhost:9245/` and `http://127.0.0.1:9245/` behave identically (both 404 with a bare
    Go client, both 200 with `Accept` sent).
  * This Vite dev server performs no Host check — `Host: evil.com` also returns 200.
* Verified the probe target itself is reachable and fast from Go: with a server bound to
  `127.0.0.1:9245`, `http.Client{Timeout: 100ms}.Get("http://localhost:9245/")` succeeds 10/10 in
  ~1ms, so the 60s budget is not the constraint.
* Isolated the difference to the request headers (table above), which led to the root cause.

Go's default `http.Client` sends no `Accept` header, the request reaches Vite without one and
Vite returns 404. `ready` is therefore never true; the loop retries every `interval` (100ms) until the
60s deadline expires, and `runCycle` then returns before it ever reaches the `Primary` step
(`process/process.go:283`).

### Suggested fix

Set an `Accept` header on the readiness request:

```go
req.Header.Set("Accept", "*/*")
```

items.title: [v3][docs] Do not present PermissionDeny as a substitute for macOS media usage descriptions

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
The permissions documentation imported by #6144 (master `2122bad44`) recommends `PermissionDeny` as a way to stop a camera/microphone request before AVFoundation is reached. That guarantee is not supported by WebKit's call order. This is a P3 documentation bug, not a request to change the runtime permission policy.

## Reproduction/evidence

1. Read the macOS caution and final macOS troubleshooting paragraph in `docs/mpress/content/features/windows/permissions.md`; the same guidance is copied into the nine locale pages.
2. Trace WebKit's media permission request path: [system validation precedes the UI delegate policy](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/b44b2cea5f88d369c0f147710c37fe0869539469/Source/WebKit/UIProcess/UserMediaPermissionRequestManagerProxy.cpp#L708-L737).
3. On Cocoa, that validation [checks and can request camera/microphone authorization](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/b44b2cea5f88d369c0f147710c37fe0869539469/Source/WebKit/UIProcess/Cocoa/UserMediaPermissionRequestManagerProxy.mm#L143-L177). The separate helpers [check usage descriptions and call AVCaptureDevice](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/b44b2cea5f88d369c0f147710c37fe0869539469/Source/WebKit/UIProcess/Cocoa/MediaPermissionUtilities.mm#L70-L85).

The source establishes that the delegate's denial is not a guarantee against earlier system authorization. A missing usage description may reject a request before the delegate; direct AVFoundation access without a required description can terminate an app. No native crash or prompt reproduction is claimed here.

Found by CodeRabbit during the #6167 master synchronization (two equivalent comments, tracked once). Searched existing issues/PRs for PermissionDeny/AVFoundation, usage-description, and requestSystemValidation: #6050/#6144 concern the original implementation, #5809 is an iOS template change, and #4270 concerns dev-mode microphone access, not this documentation guarantee.

## Scope and acceptance

- Correct the caution and troubleshooting text in the canonical page and all nine locale copies.
- Keep usage descriptions and sandbox entitlements as independent requirements; do not recommend PermissionDeny as a substitute or promise it suppresses an OS prompt.
- Retain the documented WebKit allow/deny/default behavior and avoid a runtime change.
- Refresh applicable translation audit records, run documentation validation/build and CodeRabbit, and link the prepared change here.

Scope: v3.0.0 GA/nightly documentation correction, outside the features-only v3.1.0 milestone. The correction is committed locally and awaits explicit manual push confirmation.


## Prepared correction and validation

Committed as taliesin-ai on `codex/ga-macos-permission-docs`, now `0162e464d2cd67969e4e4a6299fd10e65df63f0d` including current master `f21e67facf0a87377daaa9b1096dfc57efa489e5`. The documentation correction remains unchanged from `8d13d3f22f458e017a0879c8d0cbf696459af021`. The local worktree is clean. Nothing has been pushed and no duplicate PR has been opened.

The change corrects the macOS policy table, explanatory paragraph, caution, and troubleshooting answer in English and all nine translations. It removes the misleading workaround example and refreshes only the hashes of 27 existing platform-heading audit exceptions; no new exception was added. Runtime source is unchanged.

Validation on the final content:
- `bash docs/mpress/scripts/build.sh` passes using checksum-verified M-Press v1.0.18: all nine translation audits have zero errors; strict build produces 2,030 pages; link/asset checks and all 16 Python tests pass.
- The rendered-site check passes for 2,191 files / 2,031 HTML pages, all ten languages, and eight redirects.
- `git diff --check` passes. Ripwire's committed comparison `2122bad44..8d13d3f22` has zero structural regressions. Its call graph finds no runtime impact for these prose changes; the documentation build provides the relevant validation.
- Required `coderabbit --plain` was attempted but is unsupported by CLI 0.7.6. The supported `coderabbit review --uncommitted` completed with no findings across all 11 changed files before the commit.

Both original CodeRabbit comments are accepted and addressed by this correction. Native macOS prompt/crash behavior was not exercised; the evidence above is the source call order. This issue remains open pending publication and merge.


Previous release synchronization (2026-10-01, beta.27): This merge imports the five version/changelog files for [v3.0.0-beta.27](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/releases/tag/v3.0.0-beta.27), which releases the macOS permission-delegate fix from #6144. The pending #6018 and #6167 changelog entries are retained on their respective branches; the already-released macOS entry is removed from the unreleased file. The release files match upstream, and Go/package/lockfile versions agree. All implementation and permissions-documentation fix diffs remain unchanged.

Validation of this synchronization: `go test ./internal/version -count=1` passes; JSON/version consistency and diff checks pass. Required `coderabbit --plain` was attempted but is unsupported by CLI 0.7.6; the supported `coderabbit review --uncommitted` completed on each of the three branches, reviewing all five incoming files with no new findings. The previous review findings remain handled in the existing tracking, including the accepted documentation correction in #6204. Ripwire reports zero structural regressions for the committed release-metadata delta `012268768..52533b25d` (historical churn is unavailable in that comparison). This does not change the earlier structural findings on the recovery/Darwin code. Earlier runtime and documentation validation remains applicable to the unchanged fixes and was not rerun for this metadata-only merge.

Translation exception digests were refreshed without changing prose or exceptions.
- Legacy carousel prioritizes its first screenshot, defers later slides and reserves a stable frame while retaining autoplay. The first screenshot is lossless WebP, 91,573 → 83,722 bytes with identical decoded pixels and the existing PNG URL preserved.
- Reported primary article images receive eager/high-priority loading, asynchronous decoding and natural dimensions in current/default-v2.15.0 configured locale sources. Historical versions and inactive translations are unchanged; animated images remain animated.
- Separate M-Press engine fix: https://github.com/leaanthony/mpress/pull/7 preserves literal inline-script classes during CSS purging and adds priority hints to both hero theme images. Public CI passes; private conformance is skipped.

Repeated cold before/after tests: Chrome 151, 150ms latency, 200 KiB/s, 4x CPU, cache disabled, gzip text assets, three runs per desktop/mobile and light/dark condition, same Wails source baseline 08bdd6dac3ac02be9985170dd220afa066230635. Last observed LCP medians:

| Site | Desktop light/dark | Mobile light/dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v3 before → after | 828 → 752ms / 832 → 760ms | 804 → 728ms / 808 → 724ms |
| Legacy before → after | 2960 → 1788ms / 2956 → 1792ms | 3016 → 2068ms / 3016 → 2076ms |

The v3 measurements use released 1.0.18; they attribute only the Wails CSS integration, not an unmeasured extra gain from PR #7. Real-browser theme/no-JavaScript/animation/autoplay/stable-height checks pass. Full v3 production translation/build/link/site checks and 16 Python tests pass; all seven Docusaurus locale builds pass. CodeRabbit reviews report no findings.

Direct custom-domain requests receive a Cloudflare managed challenge (403, cf-mitigated: challenge); the public Pages deployment measured about 0.95–1.0s under the same throttling before these changes. The supplied 31-second field observation is not reproduced or attributed. Lab improvements do not establish that field outliers are fixed. No security configuration was changed.

Remaining acceptance: publish the local Wails fix after the repository-required manual confirmation, run remote CI/deploy, integrate the engine fix through its normal release gates, and collect comparable new field LCP percentiles/counts for both themes and the reported legacy URLs. Keep open until qualified. Beads mp-b52.4.12 tracks the M-Press audit side; Wails GitHub remains authoritative for Wails work.

items.title: [v3][darwin] Save dialog ignores `Filters` / `AddFilter()`: the file is saved without an extension

milestone.title: Future
milestone.description: Unscheduled feature work beyond GA. Placement here is not a commitment to a specific release. Goose should move items to a numbered milestone only when that release scope is justified.

items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.26

### Operating System

macOS

### Description

On macOS the save dialog drops its filters. `SaveFileDialogOptions.Filters` and `AddFilter()` are stored on `SaveFileDialogStruct`, but `macosSaveFileDialog.show()` never passes them to `showSaveFileDialog`, so the `NSSavePanel` is presented with no allowed content types:

- a filename without an extension comes back as is: `SetFilename("report")` with `AddFilter("PDF Document", "*.pdf")` returns `/path/report`, not `/path/report.pdf`;
- the panel accepts any extension, whatever the filters say.

Everywhere else the filters are applied:

- the macOS **open** dialog passes them to `showOpenFileDialog`;
- the Windows save dialog sets `FileFilters` and takes `DefaultExtension` from the first pattern;
- the Linux save dialog adds them to the file chooser.

Wails v2 set the save panel's allowed content types from the filters (`SaveFileDialog` in `WailsContext.m`), so an app ported from v2 starts writing files without an extension. `AddFilter()` on the save dialog is documented in `reference/dialogs.md` without a platform note.

### To Reproduce

`main.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application"
	"github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/events"
)

func main() {
	app := application.New(application.Options{Name: "save-dialog-filters"})

	app.Event.OnApplicationEvent(events.Common.ApplicationStarted, func(*application.ApplicationEvent) {
		go func() {
			path, err := app.Dialog.SaveFile().
				SetFilename("report").
				AddFilter("PDF Document", "*.pdf").
				PromptForSingleSelection()
			fmt.Printf("path=%q err=%v\n", path, err)

			app.Quit()
		}()
	})

	if err := app.Run(); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}
```

1. `go run .`
2. Press **Save** in the panel without touching the name field.

### Expected behaviour

- Expected: the returned path ends with `report.pdf`. The panel appends the extension of the first filter, as the Windows dialog does and as Wails v2 did on macOS.
- Actual: the returned path ends with `report`. `-[NSSavePanel allowedContentTypes]` of the presented panel is empty.

items.title: [v2] wailsjs file modes differ between `wails generate module` and `wails build`/`wails dev` — spurious git mode changes
items.body:
### Description

The same generated files get different permission bits depending on which command ran last:

- `wails generate module` → everything under `wailsjs/` becomes **0755** (including `.js`, `.d.ts`, `.json`)
- `wails build` / `wails dev` → `wailsjs/runtime/*` ends up **0644**, while `wailsjs/go/*` stays 0755

For projects that commit `wailsjs` (the shipped templates include it), this produces diffs with a mode change and zero content change, in both directions:

```
mode change 100644 => 100755  frontend/wailsjs/runtime/runtime.js   (after `wails generate module`)
mode change 100755 => 100644  frontend/wailsjs/runtime/runtime.js   (after `wails build`)
```

So no committed mode satisfies both commands — whichever one you commit, the other dirties the tree. The files are byte-identical; Windows is unaffected (git does not track the exec bit there).

Root cause, as far as I can trace it: two paths extract `wailsjs/runtime/`, and only the first is followed by a permission fixup.

- **Binding generation** — `v2/internal/app/app_bindings.go#L104-L123`: remove + gosod extract + `fs.SetPermissions(wailsjsbasedir, 0755)`. `fs.SetPermissions` (`v2/internal/fs/fs.go#L272-L279`) is `filepath.Walk` + `os.Chmod` without distinguishing files from directories, so regular files get the exec bit too. That comes from #1763 — not arguing it is wrong, just identifying the source of 0755.
- **Build / dev** — `generateRuntimeWrapper` (`v2/pkg/commands/build/base.go#L428-L445`, called at `#L158` from `CompileProject`): remove + gosod extract, which writes via `os.Create` → 0644, and nothing re-applies 0755 afterwards. It runs *after* the chmod above, which is why only `runtime/` flips back to 0644.

That also decides the fix, and it's your call:

- **0755 canonical** (per #1763) → apply the same permission step after `generateRuntimeWrapper`, or drop the redundant re-extract.
- **0644 canonical** → change `SetPermissions` so it only fixes up directories.

Happy to send a PR for either direction.

### To Reproduce

```bash
wails init -n modecheck -t vanilla-ts && cd modecheck

stat -c '%a  %n' frontend/wailsjs/runtime/* frontend/wailsjs/go/main/*   # all 644
wails generate module -tags webkit2_41
stat -c '%a  %n' frontend/wailsjs/runtime/* frontend/wailsjs/go/main/*   # all 755
wails build -s -tags webkit2_41
stat -c '%a  %n' frontend/wailsjs/runtime/* frontend/wailsjs/go/main/*   # runtime 644, go 755
wails generate module -tags webkit2_41
# runtime/* 755 again — flipping on every alternation
```

| step | `wailsjs/runtime/*` | `wailsjs/go/*` |
|---|---|---|
| `wails init` | 644 | 644 |
| `wails generate module` | 755 | 755 |
| `wails build` / `wails dev` | **644** | 755 |
| `wails generate module` again | **755** | 755 |

Note the first row: `wails init` writes everything 0644, so the very first `wails generate module` already turns a clean tree into five `mode change 100644 => 100755` entries.

### Expected behaviour

Both entry points leave the same permissions, so regenerating bindings is a no-op on a clean tree.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

- Searched the issue tracker, PRs and discussions for an existing report — no duplicate found.
- Traced both code paths myself and confirmed the ordering with a minimal `wails init` project (no git needed, just `stat`).
- Local workaround only: `git config --local core.fileMode false` — hides the diffs, does not fix the inconsistency.
- Considered sending a patch directly, but the intended direction (unify on 0755 vs 0644) is ambiguous because #1763 added the 0755 fixup deliberately, hence this ticket first.

### System Details

```shell

items.title: Android: time.Local does not reflect the device timezone

milestone.title: Future
milestone.description: Unscheduled feature work beyond GA. Placement here is not a commitment to a specific release. Goose should move items to a numbered milestone only when that release scope is justified.

items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.26

### Operating System

Android (experimental)

### Description

On Android, `time.Local` appears to remain incorrect in some Wails applications, even when the device timezone is configured properly.

I recently encountered this while testing a Wails v3 Android application. Dates and times were behaving as if the application was running in UTC rather than the device's configured timezone (for example `Asia/Shanghai`).

As a workaround, I manually read Android's timezone property and override `time.Local` during startup:

```go
//go:build android

package main

/*
#include <sys/system_properties.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
*/
import "C"

import (
	"time"
	"unsafe"
)

func initAndroidTimeZone() {
	cname := C.CString("persist.sys.timezone")
	defer C.free(unsafe.Pointer(cname))

	var buf [128]C.char

	n := C.__system_property_get(cname, &buf[0])
	if n <= 0 {
		return
	}

	tz := C.GoStringN(&buf[0], C.int(n))

	loc, err := time.LoadLocation(tz)
	if err != nil {
		return
	}

	time.Local = loc
}
```

After applying this workaround, time handling became consistent with the Android system timezone.

This feels like something that should ideally be handled by the runtime rather than requiring every application to implement its own Android-specific fix.

One possible improvement would be to expose the device timezone through the existing mobile bridge, similar to how APIs such as `application.Mobile.SafeAreaJSON()` are currently exposed.

For example:

```go
application.Mobile.Timezone()
```

which could internally use:

```java
TimeZone.getDefault().getID()
```

and return values such as:

```text
Asia/Shanghai
Europe/London
America/New_York
```

This would allow applications to correctly initialize `time.Local` without relying on Android system properties or custom CGO code.

I'm not sure whether this is a Wails runtime issue, a Go mobile/runtime behavior issue, or expected Android behavior, but I wanted to share the workaround and start a discussion. If this is a known limitation, perhaps exposing timezone information through the mobile bridge would be a useful addition.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a new Wails v3 application targeting Android.

2. Log the following values during startup:

```go
fmt.Println(time.Now())
fmt.Println(time.Now().Location())
fmt.Println(time.Local)
```

3. Build and run the application on an Android device configured with a non-UTC timezone (for example, Asia/Shanghai).

4. Observe that Go's local timezone may not match the device timezone.

5. Apply the workaround shown in this issue and observe that time handling becomes consistent with the Android system timezone.

### Expected behaviour

The application's local timezone should automatically match the Android device timezone.

For example, if the device timezone is set to `Asia/Shanghai`, then:

```go
time.Now().Location()

items.title: [v3] updater: CheckInterval re-downloads the whole artifact on every tick while an update is staged (StateReady)

milestone.title: Future
milestone.description: Unscheduled feature work beyond GA. Placement here is not a commitment to a specific release. Goose should move items to a numbered milestone only when that release scope is justified.

items.body:
### Wails version family
v3

### Exact Wails version
v3.0.0-beta.26 (`pkg/updater`; `updater.go` is identical on `master`)

### Operating System
All

### Description
With `Config.CheckInterval` set, every tick downloads the whole artifact again, even when an update is already downloaded, verified and waiting for `Restart` (`StateReady`). `periodicCheckLoop` only skips the tick while checking, downloading, verifying or installing:

```go
s := u.State()
if s == StateChecking || s == StateDownloading || s == StateVerifying || s == StateInstalling {
	continue
}
_ = u.CheckAndInstall(u.periodicCtx)
```

`StateReady` is not skipped, so `CheckAndInstall` runs again and re-downloads the same release. Users who postpone the restart for hours download the full release once per interval.

### To Reproduce
1. `CheckInterval: 2 * time.Second`, with a 14.6 MB artifact on a local endpoint feed.
2. Let the first check stage the update, and don't call `Restart`.
3. The feed server logs a full artifact download on every tick.

### Expected behaviour
While an update for the same version is staged (`StateReady`), the periodic check skips the download. It could still check for a newer version and download only if the version differs.

### Attempted Fixes
We leave `CheckInterval` at 0 and run our own timer that calls `Check`, then `DownloadAndInstall` only once per version.

### System Details
Windows 11 Pro 26200 (x64), Go 1.26.0, `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3 v3.0.0-beta.26`. `wails3 doctor` was not run: the test app is built with plain `go build`.

### Additional context
Also, the `Config.Window` comment says "Not yet wired in v1 of the package", but a nil `Window` does open the built-in window from `CheckAndInstall` and from periodic checks.

items.title: [v3] updater: helper exits 14 and 17 leave the app closed although the original exe is intact

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
### Wails version family
v3

### Exact Wails version
v3.0.0-beta.26 (`pkg/updater`; `helper.go` is identical on `master`, which already includes #6080)

### Operating System
Windows (the same design applies elsewhere)

### Description
In two helper failure paths the original executable is intact, but nothing is relaunched. The user is left with the app closed.

1. **Exit 14:** the target exe is held open by another process without `FILE_SHARE_DELETE` for longer than the retry window (20 × 500 ms). All swap attempts fail, then `restoreFromBackup` starts with `os.RemoveAll(target)`, which hits the same lock and fails, so the helper returns 14 without launching anything. The target was never modified.
2. **Exit 17:** the parent takes longer than 30 s to exit, for example a slow `OnShutdown`. The helper returns 17 and exits. The parent then finishes exiting, and nothing is running.

In both cases a working old exe is on disk. For the backup-copy failure, the helper already does the right thing ("The original is untouched; relaunch it instead of restoring a potentially incomplete backup").

### To Reproduce
Exit 14:
1. Start the app and stage an update.
2. From another process, open the installed exe with `CreateFile` sharing `FILE_SHARE_READ` only (no `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`), and hold it for 20 s.
3. Call `Restart()`. The helper log shows 20 failed replace attempts, then "restore failed". Exit code 14, and no app is running. With the same lock held for only 3 s, the swap succeeds on attempt 7.

Exit 17:
1. Register an `OnShutdown` that takes 35 s, then call `Restart()`.
2. The helper exits with 17 after 30 s, the app exits 5 s later, and nothing is running.

### Expected behaviour
If the target was never replaced (all swap attempts failed, or the parent timeout was hit), relaunch the original exe, or at least try to. In the exit-14 path, skip `RemoveAll(target)` when the target is still the original.

### Attempted Fixes
In our app: keep `OnShutdown` short, and run a small watchdog that relaunches the installed exe if no instance is running 60 s after `Restart`.

### System Details
Windows 11 Pro 26200 (x64), Go 1.26.0, `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3 v3.0.0-beta.26`. `wails3 doctor` was not run: the test app is built with plain `go build`.

### Additional context
Related: #6134 (Linux EXDEV, which also leaves the user with no working binary). Killing the helper at any point (0 to 1000 ms, and during the parent's `OnShutdown`) never broke the install, which is good.

items.title: [v3] updater: verification is fail-open, so unsigned releases install even when Config.PublicKey is set

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
### Wails version family
v3

### Exact Wails version
v3.0.0-beta.26 (`pkg/updater`; `verify.go` is identical on `master`)

### Operating System
All

### Description
Setting `Config.PublicKey` does not make signatures required. `runVerification` returns `nil` when the release has no `Verification` at all, or has a digest but no signature:

```go
if v == nil {
	return nil // nothing to check
}
...
if len(v.Signature) == 0 {
	return nil // digest-only mode
}
```

So with a key built in, a feed or mirror that simply leaves out the signature (or every verification field) gets its artifact installed. In our tests this was accepted with `PublicKey` set:
- a manifest artifact with only `sha256`: installed
- a manifest artifact with no verification fields: installed
- the same, with the file truncated: **a broken exe was installed**

The `Config.PublicKey` doc comment ("Strongly recommended for any app whose distribution channel might be compromised or proxied") reads as if setting the key protects against a compromised channel. It only does so if the attacker keeps the signature fields.

Related: the GitHub provider can't carry a signature at all, and with no checksum asset it installs the release unverified.

### To Reproduce
1. `Config.PublicKey` = a valid ed25519 public key, using the endpoint provider.
2. Publish a manifest for a newer version with no `signature`/`signatureAlgo` (digest only, or nothing).
3. `CheckAndInstall`: the update is staged and installed.

### Expected behaviour
When `Config.PublicKey` is set, a release without a valid signature is rejected (fail closed). An explicit opt-out could stay available for digest-only setups.

### Attempted Fixes
We now wrap the provider and reject any release without an ed25519 signature before download. That works, but it's easy to miss, and the default feels unsafe.

### System Details
Windows 11 Pro 26200 (x64), Go 1.26.0, `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3 v3.0.0-beta.26`. `wails3 doctor` was not run: the test app is built with plain `go build`.

### Additional context
Two smaller points found in the same test:
- the manifest `size` field is not checked, only used for progress
- `1.0.1-rc.1` is offered to a 1.0.0 app as newer, since there is no channel or prerelease filter

items.title: [v3] updater: failed downloads leave the temp dir behind (named-return shadows the deferred RemoveAll)

milestone.title: Future
milestone.description: Unscheduled feature work beyond GA. Placement here is not a commitment to a specific release. Goose should move items to a numbered milestone only when that release scope is justified.

items.body:
### Wails version family
v3

### Exact Wails version
v3.0.0-beta.26 (`pkg/updater`; `download.go` is identical on `master`)

### Operating System
Windows (the bug is platform-independent)

### Description
When a download fails, `Updater.download` leaves its temp directory and the partial artifact behind (`%TEMP%\wails-update-*\.artifact`), although the doc comment says "On any error every artifact created by this function (file + enclosing directory) is removed before returning."

The cause is the named results together with the deferred cleanup:

```go
func (u *Updater) download(ctx context.Context, p Provider, rel *Release) (path, dir string, err error) {
	dir, err = os.MkdirTemp("", "wails-update-*")
	...
	success := false
	defer func() {
		if !success {
			_ = os.RemoveAll(dir)
		}
	}()
	...
	return "", "", err   // sets dir = "" before the deferred func runs
```

`return "", "", err` assigns `dir = ""` before the deferred function runs, so it calls `os.RemoveAll("")`, which does nothing.

### To Reproduce
1. Serve a release whose download is cut off halfway (the server closes the connection).
2. Call `Check`, then `DownloadAndInstall`. The download fails with `unexpected EOF` (stage `download`).
3. Look in `%TEMP%`: a `wails-update-*` directory with a partial `.artifact` is left behind. This happened in 5 of 5 runs, 7.3 MB each.

Failures in the verify stage don't leak (0 of 5), and neither did a standalone "write a partial file, then delete it" test, so this is not antivirus holding the file.

### Expected behaviour
The temp directory is removed on every error path.

### Attempted Fixes
Capture the directory in a separate local for the deferred cleanup, for example `tmpDir := dir` right after `MkdirTemp` and `defer func() { if !success { _ = os.RemoveAll(tmpDir) } }()`. Or return the named values unchanged on error paths.

### System Details
Windows 11 Pro 26200 (x64), Go 1.26.0, `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3 v3.0.0-beta.26`. `wails3 doctor` was not run: the test app is built with plain `go build`.

### Additional context
Related leftovers seen in the same test: staged artifacts stay in `%TEMP%` on every path that doesn't swap (a staged update that was never applied, helper exits 13, 14 and 17, a rejected `Restart`), and the helper log `%TEMP%\wails-update-<pid>.log` is never deleted.

items.title: [v3][darwin] `mac:WindowDidUpdate` is forwarded to the page ~120 times/s and, on macOS 27, every `evaluateJavaScript:` wipes the click's transient activation — `navigator.clipboard.writeText()` rejects with NotAllowedError

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
### Wails version family v3 ### Exact Wails version v3.0.0-beta.25 ### Operating System macOS ### Description Any page action gated on *transient user activation* fails when called from a real click inside a Wails v3 window: `navigator.clipboard.writeText()` rejects with ``` NotAllowedError: The request is not allowed by the user agent or the platform in the current context, possibly because the user denied permission. ``` The click is genuine (`event.isTrusted === true`), yet `navigator.userActivation.isActive` is already `false` inside the click handler. It succeeds only on the rare click that gets lucky (see below). The same page in a Wails v2 window, or in Safari, works every time. WebAuthn (`navigator.credentials.create/get`), `window.open`, `showPicker()` and fullscreen are gated the same way and fail the same way. **WebKit half (macOS 27.0).** `WKWebView evaluateJavaScript:` runs the script as a *forced user gesture*. Since WebKit 265168@main the transient activation that grant gives is taken back when the gesture ends by calling `LocalDOMWindow::consumeTransientActivation()`, which sets the last-activation timestamp of every window in the frame tree to `-infinity` — it does not merely undo the forced activation, it also discards the activation the user's own mousedown just granted. This went unnoticed until WebKit 316338@main (2026-07-01, "Cross-Origin Iframe Can Read Clipboard via Top-Level User Interaction in Safari") made the async clipboard API require transient activation instead of `UserGestureIndicator::processingUserGesture()`. WebKit fixed the over-consumption in 321448@main (2026-09-19, https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=324512, "Regression(316338@main) 'Copy to clipboard' button on some sites sometimes does not copy the first time"), but that has not shipped in macOS 27.0. Quoting that commit: > Safari evaluates JavaScript in the page a few milliseconds after a click, so a page calling an API gated on transient activation from its click handler can find that activation already gone. […] Nothing about this is clipboard specific; any API gated on transient activation was affected. **Wails half.** Every native window event is forwarded to the page as a JS event through `evaluateJavaScript:`: - `webview_window_darwin.m` implements `windowDidUpdate:` / `windowWillUpdate:` and posts `EventWindowDidUpdate` / `EventWindowWillUpdate`. `NSWindowDidUpdateNotification` is posted from `-[NSWindow update]`, which AppKit calls for every window on every run-loop pass — it carries no data and fires after every mouse/key/timer event. - `hasListeners()` always returns true on darwin (there is a comment about this in `application.go`), so the event is queued unconditionally. - `WebviewWindow.dispatchWindowEvent` forwards every window event to JS regardless of whether the page subscribed (it carries a `TODO: Make this more efficient by keeping a list of which events have been registered and only dispatching those`). Measured in a bare app with `/wails/runtime.js` loaded: `mac:WindowDidUpdate` arrives in the page about 120 times per second while idle, and one lands within ~10 ms of every mousedown. On this WebKit each of those `evaluateJavaScript:` calls consumes the activation the mousedown granted, so by the time `mouseup`/`click` are dispatched it is gone. Trace from the page (`t` = `performance.now()` in ms): ``` mousedown active=true t=1512 event mac:WindowDidUpdate t=1513 event mac:WindowDidUpdate t=1546 … (12 more) mouseup active=false t=1840 click active=false t=1841 rejected NotAllowedError ``` Controls on the same machine: - Same page without the Wails runtime loaded (so nothing is ever `ExecJS`'d): `click active=true`, `writeText` resolves. - Runtime loaded but a single `evaluateJavaScript:` issued between mousedown and mouseup: `mouseup active=false`, `click active=false`, NotAllowedError. - Runtime loaded, `windowDidUpdate:` / `windowWillUpdate:` removed from `webview_window_darwin.m`: zero update events, `click active=true`, `writeText` resolves. Wails v2 never forwarded native window events to the page, which is why v2 apps are unaffected. ### To Reproduce `main.go`: ```go package main import ( "embed" "github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application" ) //go:embed all:assets var assets embed.FS func main() { app := application.New(application.Options{ Name: "activation", Assets: application.AssetOptions{Handler: application.AssetFileServerFS(assets)}, }) app.Window.NewWithOptions(application.WebviewWindowOptions{URL: "/"}) _ = app.Run() } ``` `assets/index.html`: ```html 


```

### Expected behaviour
