items.title: [v3][Windows] Keep abandoned WebView2 callback handlers alive until native release

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
Native validation update (2026-09-28): the [GA readiness report for #6184](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/pull/6184#issuecomment-5861114927) at `39fbbdec1b695217e5bda1876e04ed29c959657f` reports successful CLI/example builds on macOS arm64 and Windows amd64, all 51 macOS package tests passing, and Windows results of 50 passing packages plus two environment failures reproduced on master (`internal/wake`, `internal/wake/exec`, missing `sh`). The Windows edge suite, including the lifetime tests, passed according to that report, but it ran over non-interactive SSH and its live WebView2 coverage was not confirmed. Linux was offline and app launch was not tested. These are results reported by the separate native run, not tests rerun by this monitor; they do not cover the unpublished #6167 changes or the combined tree. Review/landing and the stated native coverage limits remain pending.

Implementation update (2026-09-27): #6184 now implements this lifetime fix at `39fbbdec1b695217e5bda1876e04ed29c959657f` and is tracked in v3.0.0 GA. Its PR description records native Windows reproduction and validation. The separate [integration check](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/pull/6184#issuecomment-5860742165) confirms Windows amd64/arm64 test-binary compilation and a conflict-free merge analysis with the unpublished #6167 tip. Combined native behavior remains unverified; this issue stays open while review and landing are pending. No duplicate lifetime implementation is planned.

Follow-up from reviewing the code merged by #6002 (075dded01, master 7e95d89bd), separate from the configuration/retry fixes in #6167.

## Evidence and reproduction

Chromium owns Go-allocated environment/controller/event handler objects. Native WebView2 receives their addresses through uintptr values, while Chromium.AddRef and Release both return 1 without keeping a Go reference. After replacement, the window drops the previous Chromium; after a failed/timed-out replacement, it can also drop that replacement. A pending native callback is therefore not sufficient to keep its Go handler graph reachable.

The especially relevant case is a controller/environment creation callback arriving after the initialization timeout. Closing a failed Chromium cannot close a controller/environment that has not arrived yet. The existing late-callback tests retain a Go pointer themselves, so they do not exercise collection between abandonment and Invoke.

This is a source-confirmed ownership gap, not a reproduced native crash. A deterministic Windows reproducer should delay an initialization callback beyond the timeout, abandon the instance, force GC/allocation churn, then deliver the delayed callback through its native handler address. Repeat across successful replacement and window teardown.

Go explicitly documents that uintptr does not keep an object alive: https://pkg.go.dev/unsafe. The repository's pkg/combridge already uses native-reference ownership and a Go registry; that is the existing mechanism to evaluate. A window-owned list alone does not establish callback lifetime after the window is collected and can accumulate objects after repeated successful recoveries.

## Acceptance

- Native callback ownership keeps the Go handler and implementation alive through the final native Release.
- Late callbacks after failure/timeout/close remain safe without retaining abandoned windows indefinitely.
- Tests cover forced GC, delayed Invoke, final Release, successful replacement, and teardown.
- Validate on native Windows; cross-compilation alone cannot verify the lifetime behavior.

No duplicate runtime fix was found. #5768 only changes dormant generated bindings and explicitly leaves the production pkg/edge runtime untouched.

Native verification is currently blocked in this workspace by SSH authentication to win-node1. No lifetime fix is claimed or published. Keep this Windows runtime bug in v3.0.0 GA/nightly patch scope, outside v3.1.0 features.

The two recovery failure paths discussed in PR #6002 remain in master after its merge (075dded01). The original browser/renderer crash recovery landed, but the locally prepared follow-up fixes were not included.

## Reproduction and current behavior

These are confirmed by inspecting the merged code; live fault injection for these paths has not yet been run.

1. Trigger browser-process recovery and let EmbedWithError succeed, then make a post-embed configuration COM call fail (for example GetSettings, a settings setter, background colour, or the resource filter). setupChromium(true) still calls the fatal application handler or Chromium.errorCallback, which terminates the Wails host.
2. Trigger browser-process recovery and make replacement initialization fail once. rebuildWebView shuts down the previous Chromium instance, then restores that same abandoned instance when setupChromium(true) returns false. The recovery callback clears its pending flag without scheduling another replacement; the abandoned instance suppresses ProcessFailed callbacks, so the window can remain blank until restart.

Review evidence:
- https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/pull/6002#discussion_r3999710593
- https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/pull/6002#discussion_r3999710595

- Recovery configuration errors return to the recovery caller without terminating the host; initial startup retains its existing fatal behavior.
- Close partially initialized/abandoned controllers and retry with fresh instances within the existing three-attempt budget.
- Keep the pending guard across retries, stop on teardown, and never restore an abandoned instance.
- Verify transient initialization failure followed by success, budget exhaustion, configuration HRESULT propagation, COM cleanup, and repeated close.

items.title: [v3] Windows: tray menu never opens on right-click (WM_CONTEXTMENU unhandled under NOTIFYICON_VERSION_4)

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
**Describe the bug**

On Windows, right-clicking the system tray icon never opens the menu. The icon shows, left-click and double-click work, but the menu set with `SetMenu` is silently unreachable. Linux and macOS are unaffected.

**Root cause**

`windowsSystemTray.show()` registers the icon with `NIM_SETVERSION` + `NOTIFYICON_VERSION_4`. Under version 4 the callback's `LOWORD(lParam)` delivers a right-click as **`WM_CONTEXTMENU`**, not `WM_RBUTTONUP` (NOTIFYICONDATAW docs: notification events "such as NIN_BALLOONSHOW, NIN_POPUPOPEN, or WM_CONTEXTMENU"). `wndProc` only handles `WM_RBUTTONUP`, so `rightClickHandler` never fires.

Verified on v3.0.0-beta.13 and current master (`v3/pkg/application/systemtray_windows.go`).

**To Reproduce**

Any v3 app on Windows with `app.SystemTray.New()` + `SetMenu(...)` → right-click the tray icon → nothing. Left-click still works.

**Fix**

1. Handle `WM_CONTEXTMENU` alongside `WM_RBUTTONUP` in the `wmUserSystray` switch.
2. In `openMenu()`, fall back to `GetCursorPos()` when `Shell_NotifyIconGetRect` fails or returns nil (icon sitting in the Windows 11 overflow flyout) instead of silently dropping the menu.

A PR with exactly these two changes follows.

items.title: [v3][macOS] Back-to-back Window.Close() calls crash in native windowClose (beta.25)

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
### Wails version family v3 ### Exact Wails version `v3.0.0-beta.25` (confirmed with `go run github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/cmd/wails3@v3.0.0-beta.25 version`). Also reproduced on `v3.0.0-beta.20`. The latest-beta reproduction below uses a separate module pinned to beta.25, not a local framework checkout or fork. ### Operating System macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple Silicon / arm64. ### Description Two back-to-back frontend `Window.Close()` calls for the same secondary window can terminate the entire application with a SIGSEGV in `_Cfunc_windowClose`. The standalone example below reproduces this without DCV, AWS, custom application cgo, native retain/release workarounds, MCP, window polling, or private macOS API build tags. The main window remains open, so this is not normal application termination after closing the last window. **Observed on beta.25:** the initial run and three additional runs all crashed with the same native close stack (process exit 2). Removing only the second `Window.Close()` call produced a successful control run: the secondary window closed and the main window survived until the example's intentional five-second shutdown. ### To Reproduce 1. Save the following as `main.go` in an empty directory. 2. Run: ```sh go mod init example.com/wails-double-close go get github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3@v3.0.0-beta.25 go mod tidy go build -o repro . ./repro ``` 3. The secondary window automatically requests close twice after one second. The process crashes before printing `SURVIVED five seconds`. 4. Control: remove the second `Window.Close()`, rebuild, and rerun. In my test it printed the survival message and exited normally.
Complete standalone main.go ```go package main import ( "fmt" "net/http" "time" "github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application" "github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/events" ) func main() { app := application.New(application.Options{ Name: "Double Close Repro", Assets: application.AssetOptions{Handler: http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/html") if r.URL.Path == "/secondary" { fmt.Fprint(w, `

Closing this window twice in one second.

`) return } fmt.Fprint(w, "

Main window should survive the secondary window closing.

") })}, }) app.Window.NewWithOptions(application.WebviewWindowOptions{ Name: "main", Title: "Main", URL: "/", Width: 480, Height: 240, }) app.Event.RegisterApplicationEventHook(events.Common.ApplicationStarted, func(*application.ApplicationEvent) { app.Window.NewWithOptions(application.WebviewWindowOptions{ Name: "secondary", Title: "Secondary", URL: "/secondary", Width: 480, Height: 240, }) go func() { time.Sleep(5 * time.Second) fmt.Println("SURVIVED five seconds") app.Quit() }() }) if err := app.Run(); err != nil { panic(err) } } ```
### Expected behaviour Repeated or overlapping close requests for one window should not crash the process. Once native teardown has started, another request should be safely ignored/coalesced or otherwise rejected without dereferencing an invalid native window. The documented `Close()` / `WindowClosing` API does not state that callers must prevent overlapping calls to avoid a process-level memory fault: https://v3.wails.io/reference/window/#close ### Actual behaviour / sanitized stack excerpt ```text SIGSEGV: segmentation violation signal arrived during cgo execution github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application._Cfunc_windowClose(...) github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application.(*macosWebviewWindow).close(...) pkg/application/webview_window_darwin.go:1332 github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application.webviewWindowImpl.close-fm() github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application.InvokeSync.func1() pkg/application/mainthread.go:28 github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application.dispatchOnMainThreadCallback(...) pkg/application/mainthread_darwin.go:53 ``` Local filesystem paths and irrelevant runtime addresses are omitted. ### Attempted Fixes / diagnosis **Application workaround:** process the disconnect notification only once, before requesting window closure: ```js let disconnected = false; function onDisconnect(reason) { if (disconnected) return; disconnected = true; // Existing cleanup, then Window.Close() if the user requested disconnect. } ``` This originally surfaced in a remote-desktop application: the bundled DCV SDK can synchronously notify disconnect twice for one disconnect request when data channels exist. The application incorrectly translated both notifications into a close request. That application-side duplication should be guarded, but the small example above removes the SDK entirely and reproduces the native crash. Earlier A/B checks against an actual remote session: - Both the pre-change application and its subsequent clipboard-change revision crashed on the first disconnect in native `windowClose`. - Adding only the three-line JavaScript once guard passed 20 connect/disconnect/reopen cycles, without any Go/cgo changes or native retention workaround. - These tests did not query or snapshot the closing native window. **Suspected framework race, based on source inspection:** `WebviewWindow.Close()` checks destroyed state before queuing `WindowClosing`. Event handling/listeners are asynchronous; the default close listener separately marks the window destroyed and calls the native close operation. Two requests may pass the initial check and schedule teardown twice. The native close path retains its stored `nsWindow` pointer after closing. This appears consistent with the crash, but I have not used NSZombie instrumentation to prove the Objective-C receiver's lifetime. A potential fix would need to make close initiation/teardown single-shot while preserving the documented cancellable hook semantics. I have not patched the Wails dependency. ### System Details `go run github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/cmd/wails3@v3.0.0-beta.25 doctor` completed successfully. Relevant output: ```text Wails CLI: v3.0.0-beta.25 Go Version: go1.27.1 OS: MacOS 27.0 OS build: 26A428 Platform: darwin Architecture: arm64 Apple Silicon: true CPU: Apple M3 GPU: 10 cores Memory: 16 GB CGO_ENABLED: 1 CGO_CFLAGS: CGO_CPPFLAGS: CGO_CXXFLAGS: CGO_LDFLAGS: GOARM64: v8.0 Xcode CLI: 2418 npm: 11.19.1 macOS signing: Not configured SUCCESS No issues found SUCCESS Your system is ready for Wails development! ``` The beta.25 minimal example was built with **no build tags**. The earlier beta.20 application used `private_mac_apis`; the standalone latest-beta result shows that tag is not required. The linker emitted deployment-target warnings (objects built for macOS 13/27 while linking for 11), but both the crashing example and single-close control built successfully with the same toolchain/settings. ### Additional context - Only macOS runtime behavior has been tested; I am not claiming this crash occurs on Windows or Linux. - Potentially related historical issues: #4353 (pending async callbacks after window close) and #4890 (hide/show native handle crash). This report specifically concerns duplicate close initiation and includes a current-beta standalone reproducer. - A separate diagnostic stress test previously exposed a close-versus-window-query failure in `windowZoomGet`. That is **not** the reproducer or stack reported here.

items.title: macOS: right click on an open tray menu closes and reopens it instead of being ignored

milestone.title: Future
milestone.description: Unscheduled feature work beyond GA. Placement here is not a commitment to a specific release. Goose should move items to a numbered milestone only when that release scope is justified.

items.body:
## Wails version family

v3

## Exact Wails version

`master` at 4b1f3484 (v3.0.0-beta.24 plus #6026 and #5919)

## Operating System

macOS 27.0 (26A428), arm64

## Description

A right click on the icon of an already open tray menu closes the menu and reopens it about 20 ms later, instead of being ignored. The visible result is a flicker and a menu whose state has been torn down and rebuilt. Only a left click on the icon, or a click elsewhere, actually closes it.

Observed live: "it wouldn't close when right clicked after it was already right clicked open, i had to left click the icon to close it again".

Seven occurrences in one 45 second session, every one of them a right click, none of them a left click:

```console
17:20:26.141  trace menuDidClose:
17:20:26.145  trace showMenu mouseDown: returned, menu dismissed
17:20:26.163  trace event monitor saw a status item mouse down
17:20:26.164  trace statusItemClicked: action fired
17:20:26.164  trace showMenu enqueued on the main queue
17:20:26.165  trace showMenu entering mouseDown: (blocks for the menu lifetime)
```

Close to reopen gaps: 20, 20, 20, 20, 18, 22, 23 ms.

The reopening mouse down is a real `NSEventTypeRightMouseDown`, because the local monitor installed in `systemTrayNew` matches only `NSEventMaskLeftMouseDown|NSEventMaskRightMouseDown` and it fires. Left click sessions produce no monitor line at all on macOS 27, which is consistent with the monitor never seeing a left mouse down there.

The mechanism is not confirmed. What the code shows is that `menuDidClose:` clears `statusItem.menu`, so once tracking has ended the button is back in action mode, and a right mouse down arriving after that runs `statusItemClicked:` -> `rightClickHandler` -> `ShowMenu` -> `showMenu`, which opens the menu again. What is not established is why a second right mouse down reaches the app at all after the click that dismissed the menu, and why the same does not happen for a left click. Worth checking whether the dismissing event is delivered twice.

## To Reproduce

Reproduction app: https://github.com/DefinedNet/wails/tree/b-systray-menu-tracking-repro/repros/macos-systray-updates-starved-during-menu-tracking

```
go build -o /tmp/systray-repro . && /tmp/systray-repro -open-menu-after 0 -quit-after 45s
```

1. Right click the tray icon. The menu opens.
2. Right click the tray icon again to close it. It closes and reopens immediately.
3. Left click the tray icon. It closes and stays closed.

Applying `trace.patch` from the repro prints the `menuDidClose:` / `statusItemClicked:` ordering above. The captured session is `logs/real-clicks-traced.log`.

## Expected behaviour

A right click on the icon of an already open tray menu should be ignored and the menu left open and untouched.

To be explicit about the norm here, since the first version of this report got it wrong: a system managed SwiftUI `MenuBarExtra` on this same machine and OS does not dismiss on right click either. Right click not dismissing is therefore not the defect. The defect is that Wails closes and reopens the menu rather than ignoring the click, which the trace above shows directly (`menuDidClose:` followed by a fresh `showMenu`). An intermittent run on an older build sometimes did dismiss, which a stable ignore would never do.

A minimal public `MenuBarExtra` control app will be added to the reproduction branch so this comparison can be checked independently.

## Attempted Fixes

None. This was found while measuring #6154 (tray icon and label updates are not delivered while the menu is open) and is reported separately because it looks independent of that.

items.body:
## Wails version family

v3

## Exact Wails version

`master` at 4b1f3484 (v3.0.0-beta.24 plus #6026 and #5919)

## Operating System

macOS 27.0 (26A428), arm64

## Description

`systemtray_darwin.m` hops to the main thread with `dispatch_async(dispatch_get_main_queue(), ...)` in five places: `systemTraySetLabel` (:79), `systemTraySetANSILabel` (:94), `systemTraySetIcon` (:170), `systemTrayDestroy` (:188) and `showMenu` (:204).

`showMenu` enqueues a block on the main queue. That block calls `[statusItem.button mouseDown:event]`, which blocks for the whole lifetime of the menu. The main queue is serial, so nothing else on it runs until the menu is dismissed. Every tray update issued in that window sits in the queue and is applied all at once at dismissal. The tray icon and label are frozen while the menu is open.

This is the same class of problem #6026 fixed for Go dispatched main thread work. `dispatchOnMainThread` now uses `CFRunLoopPerformBlock(kCFRunLoopCommonModes)` exactly because the main queue is not serviced during a nested loop. `SetIcon` takes two hops and only the first one was fixed: `setTemplateIcon` (systemtray_darwin.go:233) -> `dispatchOnMainThread` (delivered) -> `C.systemTraySetIcon` -> `dispatch_async` (starved).

This is not an edge case. Ordinary user clicks on both buttons were measured taking exactly this path on macOS 27.

Right click always takes it, on every macOS version: `applySmartDefaults` (systemtray.go:143-154) installs `ShowMenu` as the right click handler for every tray that has a menu, and `systrayPreClickCallback` returns 1 only when the matching handler is nil, so the monitor's native tracking path is unreachable for right click on a menu tray.

Left click is different, and this matters for reproducing. For a pure menu tray (`clickHandler == nil`, no attached window) `systrayPreClickCallback` does return 1, so on macOS 26 and earlier the monitor assigns `statusItem.menu` and native tracking is entered from the event loop rather than from a queue drain. That path does not starve. On macOS 27 the monitor never receives left mouse down at all, so the action handler runs `ShowMenu` instead and left click starves like right click. The measured sessions show this directly: the left click sessions have no `event monitor saw a status item mouse down` line, the right click sessions do.

So on macOS 26 a maintainer will reproduce this with right click but not with left click. On macOS 27 both reproduce.

## To Reproduce

Ten menu sessions opened by hand with a mouse, both buttons, macOS 27.0. Not one of them delivered a single `systemTraySetIcon` or `systemTraySetLabel` block while the menu was open; all of them arrived within 60 ms of `menuDidClose:`.

| session | button | open for | tray updates during tracking | tray updates within 60 ms of close | event monitor fired |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | left | 2.93 s | 0 | 12 | no |
| 2 | right | 2.54 s | 0 | 10 | yes |
| 3-9 | right | 0.43-0.95 s | 0 | 2-4 | yes |
| 10 | left | 0.74 s | 0 | 3 | no |

A left click session, which is the path a Desktop app takes on macOS 27:

```console
17:20:18.384  trace statusItemClicked: action fired
17:20:18.384  trace showMenu enqueued on the main queue
17:20:18.384  trace showMenu block started draining on the main queue
17:20:18.385  trace showMenu entering mouseDown: (blocks for the menu lifetime)
17:20:18.454  T+ 9.030s  mode  main run loop is in NSEventTrackingRunLoopMode at tick 36
17:20:18.454  T+ 9.030s  ran   CFRunLoopPerformBlock(common)  scheduled with tick 36, 0.000s late
17:20:21.208  T+11.783s  ran   CFRunLoopPerformBlock(common)  scheduled with tick 47, 0.000s late
17:20:21.313  trace menuDidClose:
17:20:21.314  trace showMenu mouseDown: returned, menu dismissed
17:20:21.318  trace systemTraySetIcon block ran
17:20:21.319  T+11.894s  ran   dispatch_async(main queue)  scheduled with tick 36, 2.865s late
17:20:21.319  trace systemTraySetIcon block ran
17:20:21.319  T+11.895s  ran   dispatch_async(main queue)  scheduled with tick 37, 2.615s late
```

Twelve run loop blocks were delivered on time during those 2.9 s and not one queue block. All twelve icon and label updates ran in the 9 ms after dismissal. The full log is `logs/real-clicks-traced.log` in the repro; to redo it, run the traced build with `-open-menu-after 0 -quit-after 45s` and click the tray by hand.

A self contained reproduction is available here:

https://github.com/DefinedNet/wails/tree/b-systray-menu-tracking-repro/repros/macos-systray-updates-starved-during-menu-tracking

```
go run . -interval 250ms -quit-after 12s -dismiss-after 6s
```

It creates a menu tray, alternates two template icons and a `tick N` label every 250 ms, opens its own menu through `OpenMenu()` after 3 s, and dismisses it with a posted Escape. Each tick also schedules one block through `dispatch_async(dispatch_get_main_queue(), ...)` and one through `CFRunLoopPerformBlock(kCFRunLoopCommonModes)`, and logs the current main run loop mode.

With the traced build (`trace.patch`), the essential failure is:

```console
T+ 3.051s  ran   dispatch_async(main queue)     scheduled with tick 12, 0.015s late
          trace showMenu enqueued on the main queue
          trace showMenu block started draining on the main queue
          trace showMenu entering mouseDown: (blocks for the menu lifetime)
T+ 3.293s  mode  main run loop is in NSEventTrackingRunLoopMode at tick 13
T+ 3.297s  ran   CFRunLoopPerformBlock(common)  scheduled with tick 13, 0.005s late
T+ 8.288s  mode  main run loop is in NSEventTrackingRunLoopMode at tick 33
T+ 8.293s  ran   CFRunLoopPerformBlock(common)  scheduled with tick 33, 0.005s late
          trace menuDidClose:
          trace showMenu mouseDown: returned, menu dismissed
          trace systemTraySetIcon block ran
          trace systemTraySetLabel block ran
T+ 8.321s  ran   dispatch_async(main queue)     scheduled with tick 13, 5.029s late
          trace systemTraySetIcon block ran
          trace systemTraySetLabel block ran
T+ 8.326s  ran   dispatch_async(main queue)     scheduled with tick 14, 4.791s late
```

Between tick 13 and tick 33 the run loop blocks are delivered within 5 ms each, and not one queue block, `systemTraySetIcon` or `systemTraySetLabel` runs. All 21 of them run in a burst within 40 ms of dismissal.

Without the trace patch, the same run shows 26 queue blocks landing at dismissal, the oldest 6.2 s late:

```console
T+ 9.296s  ran   dispatch_async(main queue)     scheduled with tick 12, 6.208s late
T+ 9.301s  ran   dispatch_async(main queue)     scheduled with tick 13, 6.006s late
...
T+ 9.436s  ran   dispatch_async(main queue)     scheduled with tick 33, 1.132s late
```

Visually: the counter in the menu bar froze at 11 and jumped to 38 when the menu closed.

## Expected behaviour

`SetIcon`, `SetTemplateIcon` and `SetLabel` should reach the tray while its menu is open, the way main thread work dispatched from Go does since #6026. A tray that shows connection state or a live counter should not freeze for as long as the user keeps the menu open.

## Attempted Fixes

Routing all five sites in `systemtray_darwin.m` through `CFRunLoopPerformBlock(kCFRunLoopCommonModes)` plus `CFRunLoopWakeUp`, mirroring `dispatchOnMainThread`, removes the stall in our measurements: during `NSEventTrackingRunLoopMode` the tray keeps counting and a read back of `statusItem.button.title` follows the tick. The patch is included in the repro as `cfrunloop-fix.patch`.

We are not confident it is the right fix. Patching `showMenu` alone is worse: tracking then starts inside a run loop block callout, blocks added afterwards do not run until that callout returns, and the Go caller stalls in `SetTemplateIcon` for the whole menu lifetime. Transcripts for both variants are in the repro under `logs/`.

items.body:
## Wails version family

v3

## Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.24

## Operating System

macOS

## Description

`CancellablePromise`, `CancelError`, and `CancelledRejectionError` are exported by the root `@wailsio/runtime` entry. However, importing that entry also evaluates the Wails runtime bootstrap and environment detection.

Consumers that need the real cancellation implementation without initializing the application runtime have no supported import path. This affects test and mocking infrastructure in particular.

The published package already contains standalone files for this API:

- `dist/cancellable.js`
- `types/cancellable.d.ts`

However, the package `exports` map exposes only `.` and `./plugins/*`. Importing `@wailsio/runtime/cancellable` therefore fails with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`.

This seems narrower than the invalid runtime subpaths corrected in #4989. Ordinary application APIs such as `Dialogs`, `Events`, and `Window` should use the initialized root entry. `CancellablePromise` is a pure utility that is also useful where running the runtime bootstrap is undesirable.

Would you consider exposing this already-shipped standalone module a bug fix, or a public API enhancement that should go through the WEP process?

## To Reproduce

A self-contained reproduction is available here:

https://github.com/DefinedNet/wails/tree/b-pntvuxru-cancellable-repro/repros/wailsio-runtime-cancellable-export

It installs an unmodified `@wailsio/runtime@3.0.0-beta.24` in a temporary directory and verifies that:

1. `dist/cancellable.js` and `types/cancellable.d.ts` ship in the package.
2. The root entry exports the cancellable API.
3. The standalone subpath fails with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`.
4. Adding the missing export makes the standalone subpath resolve.

The essential failure is:

```console
$ node -e "import('@wailsio/runtime/cancellable')"
Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './cancellable' is not defined by "exports" in node_modules/@wailsio/runtime/package.json
```

Importing the deep path directly also fails because the package's `exports` map is exhaustive:

```console
$ node -e "import('@wailsio/runtime/dist/cancellable.js')"
Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './dist/cancellable.js' is not defined by "exports"
```

## Expected behaviour

There should be a supported way to import the cancellation utility without evaluating the root runtime entry.

The existing published files could be exposed through this package entry:

```json
"./cancellable": {
  "types": "./types/cancellable.d.ts",
  "default": "./dist/cancellable.js"
}
```

This matches the style of the existing `.` and `./plugins/*` exports and requires no new runtime code.

## Attempted Fixes

Importing `CancellablePromise` from the supported root entry passes TypeScript checking, but it introduces runtime bootstrap side effects into our browser-based component tests.

With a local `./cancellable` export patch, our Storybook/Vitest browser suite passes:

```text
Test Files  23 passed (23)
     Tests  60 passed (60)
```

Changing only the import to the supported root entry causes timing-dependent failures during test-file collection. In one captured run:

```text
Test Files  8 failed | 15 passed (23)
     Tests  47 passed (47)
```

The individual tests that run still pass; the failures occur while collecting modules. Root-import runs evaluate the runtime environment detection at module-import time:

```text
⚠️ Browser Environment Detected

Only UI previews are available in the browser. For full functionality,
please run the application in desktop mode.
```

Observed collection errors include:

```text
Error: Vitest failed to find the runner. This is a bug in Vitest.
```

and failures to fetch dynamically imported story modules. The exact count varies because the downstream failure is timing-dependent. The deterministic upstream problem is the package-export error in the standalone reproduction.

Hand-mocking `CancellablePromise` would duplicate runtime behavior in consumer test infrastructure. A local package-export patch preserves the real implementation and avoids evaluating the root entry.

A proposed implementation with a focused manifest regression test is available here:

https://github.com/DefinedNet/wails/tree/b-pntvuxru-cancellable-export

That branch passes the runtime typecheck and all 1,208 runtime tests.

## Screenshots

Not applicable.

items.title: [v3/macOS] System tray left-click stopped working on macOS 27 (GoldenGate)
items.body:
**Wails version family:** v3

**Exact Wails version:** Wails v3.0.0-beta.24

**Operating System:** macOS

---

## Description

On macOS 27 (GoldenGate, Darwin 27), left-clicking a Wails v3 system tray icon produces no response. The menu only opens on right-click. The bug is not present on macOS 26 and earlier where left-click works as expected.

## To Reproduce

1. Build any Wails v3 app with a system tray icon and a menu
2. Run it on macOS 27 (GoldenGate)
3. Left-click the tray icon
4. Nothing happens — menu only opens on right-click or Ctrl+click

## Expected behaviour

Left-clicking the tray icon should open the menu, consistent with behaviour on macOS 26 and earlier.

## Attempted Fixes

Traced the issue to `systemTrayNew` in `v3/pkg/application/systemtray_darwin.m`. The action handler `statusItemClicked:` is never called on left-click on macOS 27 because `NSStatusItem.setTarget` / `NSStatusItem.setAction` (deprecated since macOS 10.14) stopped firing entirely in macOS 27.

Fix: set target and action directly on `statusItem.button` (the `NSStatusBarButton` modern API) instead of on the deprecated `NSStatusItem` properties. Also update the three `[statusItem target]` lookups in `systemTrayDestroy` and `showMenu` to `[statusItem.button target]`.

## System Details

- macOS 27.0 (GoldenGate), Darwin 27.0.0, Apple Silicon (arm64)
- Wails v3.0.0-beta.9

## Additional context

Confirmed working fix — tested locally on macOS 27. Will open a PR with the one-file change to `systemtray_darwin.m`.

items.title: ci(v3): duplicate permissions key prevents Build + Test workflow from running

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
Found while reviewing #6144 at commit `1e583ab8f75c294caff9e9cd22d425da74ba7bf7`.

The `Build + Test v3` workflow is rejected before any jobs start because `.github/workflows/build-and-test-v3.yml` defines the top-level `permissions` mapping twice, at lines 3 and 19. This is already present on the PR base, `master` at `2a6be718d31977381d2a57cf40ad9ef1111099a7`; it was not introduced by #6144.

Evidence:

- [Failed workflow run for the reviewed commit](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/actions/runs/35505385319): GitHub reports `(Line: 19, Col: 1): 'permissions' is already defined` and no jobs run.
- [Workflow source](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/1e583ab8f75c294caff9e9cd22d425da74ba7bf7/.github/workflows/build-and-test-v3.yml#L19).
- The green [macOS job in PR Checks (master)](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/actions/runs/35505404524/job/106064239926) runs `go test -v ./...` from `v2`, so it does not compile the v3 Objective-C bridge or execute the new Darwin permission tests in #6144.

Reproduction:

1. Inspect the workflow at the commit above and observe the duplicate top-level key.
2. Open the linked failed run and its invalid-workflow annotation.
3. Compare the available PR checks with the jobs expected from `Build + Test v3`: the v3 Go tests, macOS API variants, and v3 aggregate result have not run.

Impact and priority:

High-priority CI bug: v3 changes can show green v2 checks while the v3 validation workflow never starts. Native macOS validation for #6144 remains outstanding. This is a bug fix and should remain outside the features-only v3.1.0 milestone/project.

A second syntax error is exposed once the duplicate key is removed: `pull_request_review` does not support a `branches` filter. `actionlint v1.7.7` reports `"branches" filter is not available for pull_request_review event`. Remove that filter and retain the existing job-level `github.base_ref == 'master'` conditions.

Scope and acceptance criteria:

- Remove the duplicate mapping while preserving the intended `contents: read` permissions.
- Remove the unsupported review-event branch filter while retaining the job-level master restriction; validate the corrected workflow with actionlint.
- Confirm GitHub accepts the workflow and starts the expected v3 jobs for an applicable pull request.
- Run v3 macOS compilation and application-package tests against the commit to be merged for #6144, including `TestCaptureDecision_Constants`, `TestStrictestCaptureDecision`, `TestCaptureDecisionFor`, `TestMediaCaptureDecision`, and `TestMediaCaptureDecisionForUnknownWindow`.
- Verify the v3 build result reports the actual v3 job outcomes.

items.title: [v3] MCP `call_bound_method` loads a second runtime copy and silently stops all frontend event listeners

milestone.title: Future
milestone.description: Unscheduled feature work beyond GA. Placement here is not a commitment to a specific release. Goose should move items to a numbered milestone only when that release scope is justified.

items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.16

### Operating System

macOS

### Description

In an app that bundles `@wailsio/runtime` from npm (the standard v3 setup), a single `call_bound_method` call permanently stops every `Events.On` handler in the page from firing. Nothing raises an error: Go reports the emit as successful, the page reports the event as dispatched, and the app simply stops reacting.

`call_bound_method` evaluates `await import('/wails/runtime.js')` inside the page (`v3/pkg/application/mcp_tools_enabled.go`, ~L460). That loads a second, independent copy of the runtime, with its own empty `eventListeners` map. Its module-scope side effect in `v3/internal/runtime/desktop/@wailsio/runtime/src/events.ts:21` —

```ts
window._wails.dispatchWailsEvent = dispatchWailsEvent;
```

— overwrites the bundled copy's dispatcher, because it runs last. `inlineEventJS` then delivers every Go event into the copy that nobody subscribed to.

`js_eval`'s description recommends the same import ("The Wails runtime is importable inside the page via `await import('/wails/runtime.js')`"), so a client following the docs triggers this by hand.

### Suggested fix

Two independent changes; either one resolves the symptom.

1. **`call_bound_method` shouldn't touch the page's runtime.** The MCP server runs in the Go process that owns the bindings, so it can use `bindings.Get` + `BoundMethod.Call` — the same path `messageprocessor_call.go` uses — with the resolved window in the context. That is also faster, and works when no window is rendering (a hidden or not-yet-loaded window times out on the eval today).
2. **`events.ts` should chain rather than replace an existing dispatcher.** Any second runtime instance (a plugin, a devtools helper, an iframe sharing the window) hits this. `inline_event_shim.js` already treats an installed dispatcher as something to preserve.

Happy to open a PR for either.

### To Reproduce

1. Build any v3 app that bundles the npm runtime with `-tags mcp`, and subscribe to a custom event in the frontend.
2. Emit that event from Go. The frontend handler runs.
3. Call `call_bound_method` once, with any bound method.
4. Emit the same event again. The handler never runs. A second "Wails Runtime Loaded" line appears in the console.

A self-contained check from inside the page, with no app code involved:

```js
// Register on the app's bundled runtime and dispatch through the window's function.
const off = Events.On('probe', () => console.log('hit'));
window._wails.dispatchWailsEvent({ name: 'probe', data: null });   // "hit"

await import('/wails/runtime.js');

window._wails.dispatchWailsEvent({ name: 'probe', data: null });   // silence
```

### Expected behaviour

Calling a bound method through MCP should leave the app's event delivery working.

Testing an event-driven UI by calling a Go method and then checking that the page reacted is the pattern the tool invites — its own description is "Call a bound Go service method through the Wails runtime ... Returns the method's result." That is exactly the sequence that breaks, and it breaks silently.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

Confirmed both code paths are unchanged on `master` as of filing.

Searched the tracker for `dispatchWailsEvent`, `call_bound_method`, `runtime.js`, `_wails` and MCP (title and body) and found no existing report. #4872 / #4925 concern the opposite failure (a *missing* dispatcher after reload, a load-order race).

Workaround in our test driver: install a property accessor on `window._wails.dispatchWailsEvent` that keeps every function ever assigned to it and fans each event out to all of them. The app's copy hears events again and the MCP's copy still works. This only helps a client that knows to install it.

### System Details

```shell
# System
| Name          | MacOS        |
| Version       | 26.6         |
| Platform      | darwin       |
| Architecture  | arm64        |
| CPU           | Apple M4 Max |

# Build Environment
| Wails CLI      | v3.0.0-beta.16 |
| Go Version     | go1.26.2       |
| GOARCH         | arm64          |
| GOOS           | darwin         |

# Checking for issues
No issues found

(Dependencies and Signing sections omitted - not relevant; full output available on request.)
@wailsio/runtime npm package: 3.0.0-beta.16
```

### Additional context

Found while driving a Wails app from Claude Code over MCP for end-to-end tests. Our launcher re-reads its project list when Go announces a change; after seeding a project through `call_bound_method`, the launcher sat on "No projects yet" over a project Go had already opened. A tap on `window._wails.dispatchWailsEvent` showed every event arriving at the window while the React handler never ran.

Filing here rather than in the MCP feedback thread (#5692) since it's a reproducible bug, but happy to move it.

items.title: Linux updater helper fails across filesystems (EXDEV), strands user with no working binary

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.22

### Operating System

Linux

### Description

This is a similar issue to the Windows fix (https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/pull/5560).

On Linux, the v3 updater helper stages the verified artifact under
`os.TempDir()` (typically `/tmp/wails-update-*/`) and then calls bare
`os.Rename(newPath, target)` in `helper_unix.go:replaceTarget`. When `/tmp`
and the install directory live on different filesystems — tmpfs `/tmp` plus
persistent `$HOME` is the Arch/Fedora default — every swap attempt fails with
`EXDEV (invalid cross-device link)`. Worse than a failed update, the recovery
path then removed the working binary while failing to restore it, leaving only
`Application.bak` behind and nothing running.

Windows already handles this exact failure: PR #5560 added a rename-or-copy
fallback plus rollback to `helper_windows.go`. Linux (`helper_unix.go`) was not
changed and still uses bare rename.


My Filesystems: `/tmp` on `tmpfs`, `$HOME` on `btrfs`
  (`df -T /tmp ~` shows two different types/mounts)

helper start: target=$HOME/Applications/Application new=/tmp/wails-update-*/Application-linux-amd64 pid=...
backing up $HOME/Applications/Application → $HOME/Applications/Application.bak
replace (attempt 1): rename /tmp/wails-update-*/Application-linux-amd64 $HOME/Applications/Application: invalid cross-device link
...repeated identically through all 20 attempts...
```

End state observed on disk: only `Application.bak` remained; no working `Application`
binary and no running app.

### To Reproduce

1. Use a Linux system where `/tmp` and the install directory are on different
   filesystems (e.g. Arch/Fedora defaults: tmpfs `/tmp`, ext4/btrfs `$HOME`;
   confirm with `df -T /tmp ~`).
2. Build any Wails v3 Linux desktop app with `app.Updater` configured and a
   working provider, installed to a user-writable directory such as
   `~/Applications/`.
3. Publish a signed newer release the updater accepts (digest + signature
   verify cleanly, so the flow reaches the swap stage).
4. Trigger the update and restart into the helper.
5. Observe twenty `invalid cross-device link` attempts in
   `/tmp/wails-update-*.log`, ending with only the `.bak` file present and no
   running application.

### Expected behaviour

- The Linux helper detects the cross-device case and falls back to copy +
  fsync + delete-source, mirroring the merged Windows fix in PR #5560
  (`renameOrCopy`, mode preservation, cleanup, rollback that cannot strand
  the user).
- Alternatively, stage the artifact beside the target (same filesystem) so
  the atomic rename path holds on every layout.
- At minimum, the recovery path must never delete the working binary and
  then fail to put something runnable back: verify the replacement exists
  before removing the original, or copy the backup aside before destructive
  operations.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

## Suggested Fix

- Port the `renameOrCopy` fallback from `helper_windows.go` (PR #5560) to
  `helper_unix.go`, keyed on EXDEV (`errno 18` on Linux) rather than on every
  error, preserving the existing retry/backoff and rollback semantics.
- Consider staging the download beside the target directory when it is
  writable, so the common case stays a single atomic rename.
- Add coverage for the split-mount layout (e.g. helper tests with staging
  and target on different filesystems, or a fault-injected `replaceTarget`),
  plus an assertion that a failed swap never leaves the install directory
  without a runnable binary.

## App-Side Workaround I Shipped

Because the destructive path lives in framework code, Application now probes
the exact move at startup — rename a scratch file from `os.TempDir()` into
the executable directory, then remove it — and disables update offers with a
log line when the probe fails. That prevents strandings but leaves split-mount
users on manual tarball reinstalls; it is not a substitute for the framework
fallback above.

items.title: [v3] ICoreWebView2_N vtable structs in pkg/webview2 omit the inherited method chain, so calls hit the wrong slot

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
### Description

In `internal/webview2/pkg/webview2/`, the vtable structs for the derived `ICoreWebView2_N` interfaces embed only `IUnknownVtbl` plus the methods that interface *adds*, omitting the inherited chain. A COM vtable contains every inherited method, so calling through these structs lands on the wrong slot.

Example — `ICoreWebView2_22.go`:

```go
type ICoreWebView2_22Vtbl struct {
	IUnknownVtbl
	AddWebResourceRequestedFilterWithRequestSourceKinds    ComProc
	RemoveWebResourceRequestedFilterWithRequestSourceKinds ComProc
}
```

`AddWebResourceRequestedFilterWithRequestSourceKinds` therefore resolves to vtable slot **3**, which is `ICoreWebView2::get_Settings`. The real slot is **123**:

```
3   IUnknown
+58 ICoreWebView2
+ 7 ICoreWebView2_2      = 68
+ 5 ICoreWebView2_3      = 73
+ 4 _4, +2 _5, +1 _6, +1 _7, +7 _8, +9 _9, +2 _10, +3 _11, +3 _12,
+ 1 _13, +3 _14, +4 _15, +3 _16, +1 _17, +2 _18, +2 _19, +1 _20, +1 _21
                         = 123
+ 2 ICoreWebView2_22     = 125 slots total
```

The 68 cross-checks against `internal/webview2/pkg/edge/ICoreWebView2_2.go`, whose `iCoreWebView2_2Vtbl` does build the chain properly and has exactly 68 `ComProc` fields. The five `_3` methods likewise land at slots 69–73 in both.

The same shape appears in the other `ICoreWebView2_N.go` files in that package (`_4` … `_23`), and in some of the sibling interface files.

### Impact

As far as I can tell this package is not on the runtime path today (`pkg/edge` is what `pkg/application` uses, and its `_2`/`_3` vtables are correct), so nothing is broken for users right now. But anyone calling into these helpers gets a silent wrong-function call rather than an error.

I hit this while patching a local copy to test `AddWebResourceRequestedFilterWithRequestSourceKinds`: my first attempt copied this vtable shape, which called `get_Settings` with the filter arguments and left the asset server serving nothing, with no error anywhere. Rebuilding the full 125-slot vtable fixed the call.

### Suggestion

Either build the inheritance chain the way `pkg/edge` does (embed the parent vtable struct), or generate these files with the chain included. A cheap guard while doing so: call a known inherited method (e.g. `get_Settings`) after `QueryInterface` and check it returns `S_OK` with a non-null out-param.

Found on `v3.0.0-beta.22`.

items.title: [v3/Windows] Creating a Worker from inside a Worker fails silently when the page is served by the asset server

milestone.title: Future
milestone.description: Unscheduled feature work beyond GA. Placement here is not a commitment to a specific release. Goose should move items to a numbered milestone only when that release scope is justified.

items.body:
### Description On Windows/WebView2, creating a `Worker` **from inside another worker** fails when the page is served by the Wails asset server (`http://wails.localhost`). It fails silently: the `error` event has `message === undefined` and the event is **not** an `ErrorEvent`. The request *does* reach the asset server — the `AssetFileServerFS` log shows it being handled, with the correct `Content-Type` — but the nested worker never starts. The same code works when the page is served from a plain `http://127.0.0.1:` Go listener inside the same Wails window, and works in a stock Edge browser of the same Chromium version. This breaks every **Emscripten pthread build**, because those spawn their worker pool from inside their own worker. In my case it was [JASSUB](https://github.com/ThaUnknown/jassub) (libass): its `ready` promise simply never settles — no error, no timeout. ### Environment - Wails `v3.0.0-beta.22`, Go 1.27.0, `CGO_ENABLED=0` - WebView2 Runtime `153.0.4234.32` - Windows 11 26200 (25H2), amd64 ### Reproduction Four files, no frontend tooling: `main.go` ```go package main import ( "embed" "fmt" "io" "net/http" "os" "github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application" ) //go:embed all:frontend/dist var assets embed.FS func main() { files := application.AssetFileServerFS(assets) app := application.New(application.Options{ Name: "nested-worker-repro", Assets: application.AssetOptions{ Handler: http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { if r.URL.Path == "/report" { b, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body) fmt.Println("RESULT:", string(b)) w.WriteHeader(204) os.Exit(0) return } files.ServeHTTP(w, r) }), }, }) app.Window.NewWithOptions(application.WebviewWindowOptions{ Title: "nested worker repro", Width: 700, Height: 300, URL: "/index.html", }) if err := app.Run(); err != nil { fmt.Println(err) } } ``` `frontend/dist/index.html` ```html nested worker repro 
running…
``` `frontend/dist/parent.js` ```js const mk = (u, opts) => new Promise((res) => { const w = new Worker(u, opts) w.onmessage = () => { w.terminate(); res('ok') } w.onerror = (e) => { w.terminate(); res('FAILED (message=' + JSON.stringify(e.message) + ', isErrorEvent=' + (e instanceof ErrorEvent) + ')') } setTimeout(() => { w.terminate(); res('timeout') }, 3000) }) ;(async () => { const abs = new URL('/child.js', self.location.href).href const out = {} const r = await fetch(abs) out['fetch(child.js)'] = r.status + ' ' + r.headers.get('content-type') out['new Worker(url, {type:module})'] = await mk(abs, { type: 'module' }) out['new Worker(url) classic'] = await mk(abs, {}) out['new Worker(blob -> import url)'] = await mk(URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([`import ${JSON.stringify(abs)};`], { type: 'text/javascript' })), { type: 'module' }) out['new Worker(blob with inline source)'] = await mk(URL.createObjectURL(new Blob(["postMessage('hi')"], { type: 'text/javascript' })), {}) postMessage(out) })() ``` `frontend/dist/child.js` ```js postMessage('child alive') ``` ### Actual result ``` RESULT: { "fetch(child.js)": "200 text/javascript; charset=utf-8", "new Worker(url, {type:module})": "FAILED (message=undefined, isErrorEvent=false)", "new Worker(url) classic": "FAILED (message=undefined, isErrorEvent=false)", "new Worker(blob -> import url)": "ok", "new Worker(blob with inline source)": "ok" } ``` Note the asset server log for the same run — `/child.js` is served, the request is not lost: ``` INF [AssetFileServerFS] Handling request url=/index.html file=index.html INF [AssetFileServerFS] Handling request url=/parent.js file=parent.js INF [AssetFileServerFS] Handling request url=/child.js file=child.js INF [AssetFileServerFS] Handling request url=/child.js file=child.js ``` So: a **top-level** worker created from the document loads fine (`/parent.js`), and `fetch()` of the child script from inside that worker returns 200 with the right MIME — only `new Worker(url)` *from inside a worker* fails. ### Expected result All five entries `ok`, as they are when the same page is served from a plain `http://127.0.0.1:` listener (verified in the same Wails window by pointing `WebviewWindowOptions.URL` at a Go `http.Server` on loopback), and as they are in stock Edge 153 on a plain http origin. ### Things I ruled out - **System proxy.** I had a proxy configured whose bypass list does not cover `wails.localhost`. Tested `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--no-proxy-server` and `--proxy-bypass-list=*.localhost;;127.0.0.1` — no change. - **MIME type.** `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`, as shown above. - **`WebResourceRequested` request source kinds.** `webview_window_windows.go` calls the deprecated `AddWebResourceRequestedFilter("*", COREWEBVIEW2_WEB_RESOURCE_CONTEXT_ALL)`, which has no `RequestSourceKinds` parameter, so I assumed worker-sourced requests were simply not filtered. I patched a local Wails copy to call `AddWebResourceRequestedFilterWithRequestSourceKinds("*", CONTEXT_ALL, SOURCE_KINDS_ALL)` via `ICoreWebView2_22` instead (and also tried registering both filters). The call succeeds, but **nested workers still fail**. So that is not the cause — though switching to the non-deprecated overload may still be worth doing on its own. ### Workaround Replacing `globalThis.Worker` inside the parent worker so that a URL becomes a blob which merely *imports* the absolute URL: ```js const NativeWorker = globalThis.Worker globalThis.Worker = class extends NativeWorker { constructor(url, opts = {}) { let u = String(url) if (!/^(blob:|data:)/.test(u)) { const abs = new URL(u, self.location.href).href const src = opts.type === 'module' ? `import ${JSON.stringify(abs)};` : `importScripts(${JSON.stringify(abs)});` u = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([src], { type: 'text/javascript' })) } super(u, opts) } } ``` The blob must only *forward* to the absolute URL, not inline the source — otherwise `import.meta.url` becomes the `blob:` URL and Emscripten's `new Worker(new URL("...", import.meta.url))` throws `Invalid URL`. With this shim injected into JASSUB's worker bundle, libass initialises and renders correctly on `wails.localhost` (8 libass threads, identical output to the loopback-origin run). ### Note This may well be a WebView2 limitation rather than something Wails does wrong — I have not been able to determine which side drops the response. But it is invisible to the developer (no error message at all) and it silently breaks any threaded wasm library, so it seems worth documenting even if the fix has to come from upstream.

items.title: v3 setup: finish the wizard server lifecycle and show system details

labels.name: WIP
labels.description: The issue is currently under development

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
## Problem

The setup wizard's final screen offers only **Start Building**, which opens documentation; it does not call the existing completion endpoint or explain how to stop the local server. The dependency check also collects basic system information without displaying it.

Reported in [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/1042734330029547630/1065600636294549514/1549029437356384321) on 2026-09-14. Related feedback tracker: #4904. The reporter did not specify a platform or version.

## Reproduction

1. Run `wails3 setup` and complete the dependency check.
2. Observe that the result screen has no system/environment summary.
3. Finish or skip the remaining configuration steps.
4. Click **Start Building** on the final screen: documentation opens, but the setup server continues running with no completion/stop action or Ctrl+C guidance.

## Scope and acceptance criteria

- [x] Automatically finish setup when leaving the final page, closing its tab, or selecting **Start Building**, while retaining the explicit finish action.
- [x] Let background Docker builds finish before stopping the server; explain this when finishing setup.
- [x] Surface request failures and provide Ctrl+C guidance rather than claiming success.
- [x] Display detected OS/version, architecture, CPU/GPU/memory when available, platform environment details, and Go/Wails versions after dependency checks, including when dependencies are missing.
- [x] Reuse doctor's system collection, preserve existing doctor output, and tolerate unavailable optional hardware details.
- [x] Rebuild embedded wizard assets and verify shutdown and frontend behavior.

Priority: P3 (onboarding usability; setup itself succeeds). Keep this combined feedback ticket outside v3.1.0 because it includes the broken completion flow; that fix is suitable for a nightly patch.


## Implementation status

Implemented and verified locally; changes are uncommitted and have not been pushed. Keep this issue open until the fix lands.

- Added automatic completion on final-page exit/tab close and **Start Building**, plus **Finish setup**, success/retry feedback, and terminal Ctrl+C guidance. Completion uses POST, tolerates retries, and waits for background Docker builds. Build registration now happens before exposing its running status.
- Reused `doctor.CollectSystemInfo()` to populate a collapsible system/environment panel on both dependency result screens. Optional hardware details may be absent.
- Prevented navigation back into the wizard after reaching completion and disconnected the background status stream when finishing.
- Rebuilt the embedded setup wizard frontend assets.

Validation:
- `go test -race ./internal/setupwizard ./internal/doctor` passed on Linux, including new completion and system-state regression tests.
- `npm run build` passed (TypeScript and production bundle).
- Setup wizard test binaries cross-compiled for Windows amd64 and macOS arm64; native execution on those platforms was not performed.
- Chromium checks against the production frontend with mocked API responses passed: ready/missing dependency summaries, finish POST, server-error retry, ordinary completion, and completion with a background Docker build.
- `git diff --check` passed. Ripwire contract checks reported no incompatible callers; its quality report retained heuristic clone findings on unchanged fetch helpers and flagged inherited hardware-collection complexity. Its suggested Go test packages were run; frontend behavior was checked in Chromium.



### Automatic shutdown follow-up (2026-09-15)

The final screen listens for `pagehide` and sends a completion POST using `sendBeacon`, falling back to a keepalive fetch if the beacon cannot be queued. Earlier screens and ordinary tab switching do not trigger completion. React effect cleanup only removes the listener, avoiding premature shutdown during StrictMode remounts. **Start Building** also completes setup when opening the documentation. Acknowledged completion removes the exit listener.

Verified in Chromium with an actual local HTTP server receiving the requests: leaving the final page, closing its tab, beacon fallback, and **Start Building** each deliver a completion POST; closing an earlier screen delivers none. The TypeScript/production build, Go race tests for setupwizard and doctor, and whitespace checks pass. Embedded frontend assets are rebuilt. Changes remain uncommitted and unpushed.

items.title: [v3] MSIX packaging fails for newly created projects
items.body:
## Description

MSIX packaging is broken for newly created Wails v3 projects. This has been reproduced and independently confirmed during GA triage.

A fresh project can be built, but the generated Windows packaging workflow does not produce a usable MSIX package. This blocks Windows developers from shipping a new application through the MSIX path.

## Reproduction

On Windows:

1. Create a new project with the current Wails v3 CLI.
2. Enter the generated project directory.
3. Install the MSIX tooling if required with `wails3 task install:msix:tools`.
4. Run the generated MSIX packaging workflow with `wails3 task package FORMAT=msix`.

## Expected behaviour

The generated task builds the application and creates a valid MSIX package in the project output directory.

## Actual behaviour

The MSIX packaging step fails for a freshly generated project, so no distributable MSIX package is produced.

## Impact

This is a Windows packaging show-stopper for GA: the out-of-box new-project workflow cannot produce an MSIX release artifact.

## Investigation notes

- Reproduce against a completely fresh project to exclude migrated Taskfile or build-asset customisations.
- Capture the exact failing command and output from the generated `create:msix:package` task.
- Verify both supported Windows architectures and the default MakeAppx path.
- Add an end-to-end smoke test that initializes a project and packages it as MSIX on Windows.

items.title: [v3] window._wails.environment is never set on Android or iOS, so System.IsAndroid()/IsIOS() always return false

milestone.title: Future
milestone.description: Unscheduled feature work beyond GA. Placement here is not a commitment to a specific release. Goose should move items to a numbered milestone only when that release scope is justified.

items.body:
## Summary

`window._wails.environment` is only ever populated by `runtime.Core()`, which is injected from the three desktop webview backends. On Android and iOS `Core()` is never called, so the object is missing entirely — and the public runtime API that reads it always answers "no":

```ts
// internal/runtime/desktop/@wailsio/runtime/src/system.ts:138
export function IsAndroid(): boolean {
    return (window as any)._wails?.environment?.OS === "android";
}
```

`System.IsAndroid()` returns `false` on Android, and `System.IsIOS()` returns `false` on iOS.

## Where the value comes from

`window._wails.environment` is written in exactly one place:

```go
// internal/runtime/runtime_dev.go:10  (runtime_prod.go:8 is the same with Debug:false)
var environment = fmt.Sprintf(`window._wails.environment={"OS":"%s","Arch":"%s","Debug":true};`, runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH)
```

and concatenated into the runtime prelude in `internal/runtime/runtime.go:21`:

```go
return runtimeInit + flagsStr + invoke + environment + runtimeConfigReady
```

That prelude is built by `runtime.Core(...)`, and `Core(` has exactly three callers, all desktop:

- `pkg/application/webview_window_darwin.go:1459`
- `pkg/application/webview_window_linux.go:444`
- `pkg/application/webview_window_windows.go:2672`

Neither `application_android.go`, `application_android_nocgo.go` nor `application_ios.go` mentions `Core(` or `_wails.environment`.

## Confirmed on device

Read-only probe (a single `evaluateJavascript` in `onPageFinished`, no behaviour change), physical Android 16 / API 36 arm64-v8a device, Wails v3 app:

```
D/WailsProbe: ENV_PROBE="{...\"hasUnderscoreWails\":true,\"environment\":null,\"flags\":null}"
```

(excerpt — the probe reports several fields.) `window._wails` exists and the bridge is live, but both `environment` and `flags` are `null`.

## Impact

`System.IsAndroid()` / `System.IsIOS()` are the documented way to branch on platform, and they cannot return true on the platform they name. The same key is read in at least two more places: `appregion.ts:217` and `drag.ts:46`.

Worth noting this is a wrong-answer API rather than a dead runtime: on Android the transport is selected from the presence of the JavaScript bridge (`runtime.ts:239`, keyed off `window.wails.invokeAsync`), not from `environment` — so apps still work, which is presumably why this has gone unnoticed.

## Suggested direction

Desktop receives this through a prelude injected before page scripts run; mobile has no equivalent. On Android `androidx.webkit` is already a dependency (`androidx.webkit:webkit:1.9.0` in the Android build template), so `WebViewCompat.addDocumentStartJavaScript` is the natural place to inject the same prelude, with a fallback for WebViews that do not support `DOCUMENT_START_SCRIPT`. iOS would need the equivalent in the WKWebView setup.

Happy to prepare a PR — I would rather agree on the mechanism first, since it touches the mobile WebView setup on both platforms. If you consider the fix a change to public behaviour rather than a bug fix, say the word and I will open a WEP instead.

items.title: [v3] InvokeSync* never returns when the dispatched callback panics: wg.Done() is skipped by the recovering handlePanic

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
### Description

All five `InvokeSync*` variants in `v3/pkg/application/mainthread.go` call `wg.Done()` as the last statement of the dispatched closure instead of deferring it, while `defer handlePanic()` sits above it:

```go
func InvokeSync(fn func()) {
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	wg.Add(1)
	globalApplication.dispatchOnMainThread(func() {
		defer handlePanic()
		fn()
		wg.Done()      // skipped when fn() panics
	})
	wg.Wait()          // blocks forever
}
```

`handlePanic` calls `recover()` and returns normally (`v3/pkg/application/panic_handler.go`), so a panic inside `fn` is swallowed and the closure unwinds cleanly — but `wg.Done()` never runs, and `wg.Wait()` blocks for the life of the process.

The recovery is the trap. Because the panic is handled rather than propagated, the process keeps running and there is no crash to point at: the caller is simply wedged forever, with a healthy-looking application around it.

Affected on `main` today (`mainthread.go`): `InvokeSync` :23, `InvokeSyncWithResult` :34, `InvokeSyncWithError` :46, `InvokeSyncWithResultAndError` :58, `InvokeSyncWithResultAndOther` :70. `InvokeAsync` :82 is correct — it has no WaitGroup.

**Application code cannot work around this.** The `sync.WaitGroup` is a local variable inside the Wails function; there is no handle a caller could use to release it. The only remedies available downstream are to guarantee no callback ever panics, or to avoid `InvokeSync*` entirely.

### Where it bites hardest

A panic handler that wants to show UI. On Linux, `linuxDialog.show` wraps its work in `gtkDispatch`, which in the default build (`gtkdispatch_linux.go`, `//go:build linux && !gtk3 && !android && !server`) is an unconditional goroutine, and `runQuestionDialog` marshals to the main thread with `InvokeAsync` and blocks on its result channel. If anything on that path panics, the GTK main thread is parked in `wg.Wait()` and no dialog can ever be drawn again.

The practical consequence for us: a crash dialog that should let the user send a crash report cannot render, so a panic on Linux produces no report and no visible explanation — the window just disappears.

### To Reproduce

```go
package main

import (
	"time"

	"github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application"
)

func main() {
	app := application.New(application.Options{Name: "invokesync-panic"})
	app.Window.NewWithOptions(application.WebviewWindowOptions{})

	go func() {
		time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
		application.InvokeSync(func() {
			panic("boom")
		})
		// unreachable: InvokeSync never returns
		println("InvokeSync returned")
	}()

	_ = app.Run()
}
```

Expected: the panic is handled and `InvokeSync` returns, printing `InvokeSync returned`.
Actual: the panic is logged by `handlePanic`, the goroutine is wedged in `wg.Wait()` forever, and the line never prints. The same happens for the four other `InvokeSync*` variants.

### Expected behaviour

`InvokeSync*` returns after a recovered panic in the callback, releasing the caller. A panic in dispatched work should not permanently block the caller, and on the platforms where the dispatch is inline it should not strand the main thread.

### Attempted Fixes

Deferring the release fixes all five. Note the ordering: because deferred calls run LIFO, `wg.Done()` should be deferred **first** so that `handlePanic` still runs before the caller is released.

```go
	globalApplication.dispatchOnMainThread(func() {
		defer wg.Done()
		defer handlePanic()
		fn()
	})
```

I verified both orderings in a standalone probe that mirrors the closure shape with a stub `handlePanic` that recovers and returns:

| shape | panicking callback | normal callback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| current (`wg.Done()` last statement) | caller never released | released |
| `defer handlePanic()` then `defer wg.Done()` | released, but *before* the panic is processed | released |
| `defer wg.Done()` then `defer handlePanic()` | released *after* the panic is processed | released |

`recover()` still works in the last shape — both calls are deferred directly by the closure that panics.

One deliberate semantic change worth calling out: for the variants that assign a result, a callback that panics before its assignment completes will now return the zero value to the caller instead of blocking forever. That is the point of the change, but it does mean a caller that previously hung will now proceed with a zero value, so it is a behavioural change rather than a pure bug fix.

Happy to open a PR with this plus a regression test if the shape looks right to you.

### System Details

Found while investigating why a Linux crash dialog never renders. Verified by reading `main` rather than only the pinned release: the code is identical in `v3.0.0-beta.19` (latest published) and on `main` at the time of filing. Reproduced against `v3.0.0-beta.19`.

### Additional context

I searched open and closed issues and PRs for this before filing and found nothing covering it. #6026 (`fix(v3): keep serving main thread work on macOS while a modal loop runs`) touches only `mainthread_darwin.go` and the darwin harness, not the shared `InvokeSync*` bodies. #5107 fixes a different deadlock (an `RLock` held across `InvokeSync`).
